definition_zh: 阴凉处；色调；灯罩；遮挡光线
definition_en: an area away from direct sunlight, a particular degree of colour, a cover that softens a light, or to shelter something from light
core_image: 树冠下的一块暗地，光斑在草叶上晃动
scene: 我们坐在树荫下。 We sat in the shade of a tree.
sceneCN: 这里 shade 是「阴凉处」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我们坐在树荫下。

senses.title: Area out of sunlight
senses.definition: a place where direct sunlight is blocked
senses.definitionCN: 直射阳光被挡住的地方
senses.example: We sat in the shade of a tree.
senses.exampleCN: 我们坐在树荫下。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most common sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老、最常见的义项。

senses.title: Degree of colour
senses.definition: a particular degree or variety of a colour
senses.definitionCN: 颜色的某种深浅或变化
senses.example: The walls are a pale shade of blue.
senses.exampleCN: 墙壁是淡蓝色调。
senses.why: Darkness and colour are both degrees of light.
senses.whyCN: 暗度与颜色都是光的程度。

senses.title: Lamp cover
senses.definition: a cover that softens or directs a light
senses.definitionCN: 使光线变柔或改变方向的罩子
senses.example: She bought a new lamp shade.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一个新灯罩。
senses.why: A shade controls light indoors.
senses.whyCN: 灯罩在室内控制光线。

senses.title: To block light
senses.definition: to shelter something from direct light
senses.definitionCN: 使某物免受直射光
senses.example: The trees shade the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 树木为花园遮阴。
senses.why: The noun becomes the action.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动作。

intro.en: Shade comes from Old English sceadu, shadow, and is closely related to shadow.
intro.cn: shade 源自古英语 sceadu（影子），与 shadow 关系密切。

items.en: Skadwo meant shadow.
items.cn: skadwo 意为影子。

items.en: Sceadu meant shade or shadow.
items.cn: sceadu 意为阴凉或影子。

items.en: Shade named shelter from the sun.
items.cn: shade 指遮阳的阴凉处。

items.en: Shade named degrees of colour.
items.cn: shade 指颜色的深浅。

items.en: Shade named a lamp cover.
items.cn: shade 指灯罩。

note.en: Shade is compared with similar-looking words and with words for shadow and colour.
note.cn: 把 shade 与形近词以及表示影子和颜色的词作比较。

entries.definition: a dark shape cast by an object

normalIntro.en: Shade is light held back: under a tree, inside a colour, over a lamp.
normalIntro.cn: shade 是被挡住的光：在树下、在颜色里、在灯上。

normal.en: The dog slept in the shade.
normal.cn: 狗在阴凉处睡觉。

normal.en: The sofa is a darker shade of grey.
normal.cn: 沙发是更深一层的灰色。

normal.en: The lamp shade is made of paper.
normal.cn: 灯罩是纸做的。

normal.en: A large tree shades the road.
normal.cn: 一棵大树为道路遮阴。

normal.en: There are many shades of meaning here.
normal.cn: 这里有意义上的许多细微差别。

abstract.en: Shade is the shape light leaves when it is interrupted.
abstract.cn: 阴凉，是光被打断后留下的形状。

abstract.en: Every colour is a small decision about how much light to keep.
abstract.cn: 每一种颜色，都是关于保留多少光的小决定。

abstract.en: Rest often happens just outside the brightest place.
abstract.cn: 休息，常常发生在最亮处之外。

examples.en: We sat in the shade of a tree.
examples.cn: 我们坐在树荫下。

examples.en: The walls are a pale shade of blue.
examples.cn: 墙壁是淡蓝色调。

examples.en: She bought a new lamp shade.
examples.cn: 她买了一个新灯罩。

dict_mnemonic.text: shade 源自古英语 sceadu（影子），核心义「光被挡住的地方」，引申出色调与灯罩。

root: 源自古英语 sceadu（影子、阴凉），与 shadow 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Shade means a cool dark place, a degree of colour, a lamp cover, or to block light.
sensesIntro.cn: shade 意为阴凉处、色调、灯罩或遮挡光线。

core.en: Light partly blocked, creating rest or tone.
core.cn: 光被部分挡住，产生阴凉或色调。

branches.en: A cool place out of the sun.
branches.cn: 避开阳光的阴凉处。

branches.en: A degree of a colour.
branches.cn: 颜色的一种深浅。

branches.en: A cover over a light.
branches.cn: 罩在灯上的罩子。

branches.en: The act of blocking light.
branches.cn: 挡住光的动作。

branches.en: The place and the action share a word.
branches.cn: 地方与动作共用一个词。

intro.en: Shade is a native Germanic word that builds shadow and shady.
intro.cn: shade 是日耳曼语本族词，衍生出 shadow 与 shady。

latinIntro.en: Shade has no Latin ancestor; Latin umbra, shadow, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shade 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 umbra（影子）只是语义对应词。

items.example: They ate at a shaded table.
items.exampleCN: 他们在一张有遮阴的桌旁吃饭。

items.example: We rested on a shady bench.
items.exampleCN: 我们在阴凉的长椅上休息。

items.meaning: a dark shape cast by light
items.example: The shadow moved with the sun.
A shadowy figure stood at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 一个朦胧的身影站在门口。
这个消息让聚会黯然失色。

definition_en: the part of a garment that covers the arm, or a tube that covers something
core_image: 长袖衬衫的袖口整齐地卷起
scene: 天冷了，把袖子放下来吧。 It is cold, so pull your sleeves down.
sceneCN: 这里 sleeve 是「袖子」（第 1 个义项）；句意：天冷了，把袖子放下来吧。

senses.title: The arm cover
senses.definition: the part of a piece of clothing that covers all or part of the arm
senses.definitionCN: 衣物覆盖全部或部分手臂的部分
senses.example: It is cold, so pull your sleeves down.
senses.exampleCN: 天冷了，把袖子放下来吧。
senses.why: This is the clothing sense everyone knows.
senses.whyCN: 这是人人皆知的服装义项。

senses.title: A protective tube
senses.definition: a tube that covers and protects a part
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖并保护某个部件的管子
senses.example: The cable is protected by a plastic sleeve.
senses.exampleCN: 电缆由塑料套管保护。
senses.why: The shape of a sleeve fits tubes and covers.
senses.whyCN: 袖子的形状适合管子和套子。

senses.title: The record cover
senses.definition: a paper or card cover for a record
senses.definitionCN: 唱片的纸质或卡纸封套
senses.example: The sleeve was signed by the band.
senses.exampleCN: 封套上有乐队的签名。
senses.why: A cover wraps a record as a sleeve wraps an arm.
senses.whyCN: 封套包住唱片，就像袖子包住手臂。

intro.en: Sleeve is an old English word for a garment's arm cover.
intro.cn: sleeve 是英语中表示衣物手臂部分的古老词。

items.en: Sliefe named the arm of a garment.
items.cn: sliefe 指衣物的手臂部分。

items.en: The form shifted to sleve.
items.cn: 词形演变为 sleve。

items.en: The spelling settled as sleeve.
items.cn: 拼写最终定型为 sleeve。

items.en: The word named protective tubes.
items.cn: 这个词也用来指保护性套管。

items.en: It came to mean a record cover.
items.cn: 它开始表示唱片封套。

note.en: Sleeve is compared with look-alike words and words for covers.
note.cn: 把 sleeve 与形近词以及表示覆盖物的词作比较。

entries.definition: to go away from a place
the limb from shoulder to hand

normalIntro.en: A sleeve is a tube of cloth for an arm.
normalIntro.cn: sleeve 是给手臂的布料圆筒。

normal.en: It is cold, so pull your sleeves down.
normal.cn: 天冷了，把袖子放下来吧。

normal.en: The cable is protected by a plastic sleeve.
normal.cn: 电缆由塑料套管保护。

normal.en: The sleeve was signed by the band.
normal.cn: 封套上有乐队的签名。

normal.en: He rolled up his sleeves and started work.
normal.cn: 他卷起袖子开始干活。

normal.en: She wore a shirt with short sleeves.
normal.cn: 她穿了一件短袖衬衫。

abstract.en: Rolling up your sleeves is a promise to begin.
abstract.cn: 卷起袖子是开始的承诺。

abstract.en: A sleeve holds the arm without holding it back.
abstract.cn: 袖子容纳手臂，却不束缚手臂。

abstract.en: Some things are kept in covers, some in courage.
abstract.cn: 有些东西放进封套，有些放进勇气。

examples.en: It is cold, so pull your sleeves down.
examples.cn: 天冷了，把袖子放下来吧。

examples.en: The cable is protected by a plastic sleeve.
examples.cn: 电缆由塑料套管保护。

examples.en: The sleeve was signed by the band.
examples.cn: 封套上有乐队的签名。

dict_mnemonic.text: sleeve 与 slave 形近；roll up one's sleeves 是「卷起袖子、准备大干」，sleeveless 是「无袖的」。

root: 源自古英语 sliefe（衣袖）；核心义「包住手臂的筒状部分」，引申为套筒和封套。

sensesIntro.en: Sleeve means the arm of a garment, a protective tube, or a record cover.
sensesIntro.cn: sleeve 意为衣袖、保护性套管，或唱片封套。

core.en: A tube of material that wraps something.
core.cn: 包裹某物的筒状材料。

branches.en: Cloth follows the line of the arm.
branches.cn: 布料顺着手臂的线条。

branches.en: A tube protects a cable.
branches.cn: 套管保护电缆。

branches.en: Paper wraps a record.
branches.cn: 纸包住唱片。

branches.en: Garment and tube share a shape.
branches.cn: 衣物与管子共享一种形状。

branches.en: Both protect what they contain.
branches.cn: 两者都保护所装的东西。

intro.en: Sleeve forms words for arms and protective covers.
intro.cn: sleeve 构成表示手臂和防护套的词。

latinIntro.en: Sleeve is Germanic in origin, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: sleeve 源自日耳曼语，并非拉丁语。

items.meaning: the arm cover of a garment

items.exampleCN: 她穿了一条无袖连衣裙。

items.meaning: having sleeves of a stated kind

items.example: He wiped his hands on his shirt sleeve.
Wear long sleeves in the sun.
They rolled up their sleeves and cleaned.
items.exampleCN: 他们卷起袖子开始打扫。

definition_en: a way of thinking about something, or a position from which something is seen
core_image: 两个人在山的两侧，看到不同的坡
scene: 讨论会上，工程师和村民对同一个水坝各说各话，因为他们的立场完全不同。 From a farmer’s viewpoint, the dam is a threat rather than a promise.
sceneCN: 这里 viewpoint 是「观点、立场」（第 1 个义项：思考某事时所处的角度）；句意为从农民的角度看，这座水坝是威胁而非希望。山两侧看到不同坡面的两个人正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 合成词的前半部分，义为「看法；景色」
合成词的后半部分，义为「点；位置」
加后缀 -ed 构成，义为「带有特定立场的」（少数用法）

senses.title: A way of thinking about a matter
senses.definition: a particular attitude or set of opinions on a subject
senses.definitionCN: 对某一问题所持的态度或一套看法
senses.example: From a farmer’s viewpoint, the dam is a threat rather than a promise.
senses.exampleCN: 从农民的角度看，这座水坝是威胁而非希望。
senses.why: View gives what one sees and point gives where one stands; together they name the place a judgment comes from.
senses.whyCN: view 给的是所见，point 给的是所站之处；合起来就指判断出自的那个位置。

senses.title: A physical position for observing
senses.definition: the spot from which a scene or object is looked at
senses.definitionCN: 观看某一场景或物体时所处的地点
senses.example: The guide marked the best viewpoint above the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 导游标出了山谷上方最好的观景位置。
senses.why: A painter must choose an eye-level before starting, and that place is literally a viewpoint.
senses.whyCN: 画家动笔前要选定视平线所在的位置，那正是字面意义上的 viewpoint。

senses.title: The angle shown in a picture or film
senses.definition: the camera angle from which a scene is filmed or drawn
senses.definitionCN: 拍摄或绘制场景时所用的机位角度
senses.example: The scene is shot from a child’s viewpoint.
senses.exampleCN: 这场戏是从一个孩子的视角拍的。
senses.why: Film borrows the word to name the eye the camera pretends to be.
senses.whyCN: 电影借用这个词，指镜头假装成为的那只眼睛。

senses.title: In debate, one side of an argument
senses.definition: one of the positions presented in a discussion or dispute
senses.definitionCN: 讨论或争执中所呈现的一个立场
senses.example: Each viewpoint was given ten minutes in the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论中每一方立场各给十分钟。
senses.why: When positions are counted and timed, the abstract angle becomes a labelled side.
senses.whyCN: 当各方立场被计数并分配时间时，抽象的角度就成了一条标名的立场。

senses.title: A standpoint supported by evidence
senses.definition: an opinion backed by facts or experience rather than feeling
senses.definitionCN: 以事实或经验为依据而非仅凭感觉的意见
senses.example: Her viewpoint rests on five years of field data.
senses.exampleCN: 她的看法建立在五年实地数据之上。
senses.why: The word suits arguments that can point at something, since point is inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词适合能指向具体证据的论证，因为它本身就含着 point。

intro.en: Viewpoint is an English compound: view, what is seen, plus point, a place.
intro.cn: viewpoint 是英语合成词：view（所见）加 point（位置）。

items.en: Veue, a seeing, reached English as view.
items.cn: 古法语 veue（看见）进入英语成为 view。

items.en: Punctum meant a small hole or a dot, from pungere, to prick.
items.cn: punctum 意为小孔或小点，源自 pungere（刺）。

items.en: French point named a dot or a place on a surface.
items.cn: 法语 point 指平面上的点或位置。

items.en: The compound viewpoint joined the two words for a judging position.
items.cn: 合成词 viewpoint 把两个词合成表示判断的位置。

items.en: It spread from painting and surveying to opinion writing.
items.cn: 它从绘画与测量扩展到议论文章。

note.en: The first group holds the two words that make the compound plus its relatives, the second the near synonyms for opinion.
note.cn: 第一组是构成这个合成词的两个词及相近形式，第二组是「意见」的近义词。

entries.definition: the position from which one judges
a way of seeing things in proportion
the direction from which a thing is approached

normalIntro.en: Two plain words welded together: where you view from is what you point at.
normalIntro.cn: 两个普通词焊在一起：从哪里看，就指向什么。

normal.en: Viewpoint is view plus point, and the stress falls on view.
normal.cn: viewpoint 是 view 加 point，重音落在 view。

normal.en: Standpoint is its close twin, made with stand.
normal.cn: standpoint 是它的近义双胞胎，用 stand 构成。

normal.en: It takes from: from my viewpoint.
normal.cn: 前面常接 from：from my viewpoint。

normal.en: The plural simply adds s: viewpoints.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s：viewpoints。

normal.en: Point at the end hints that reasons can be pointed to.
normal.cn: 结尾的 point 提示理由是可以指出的。

abstract.en: Picture two hikers on opposite slopes, each seeing one side.
abstract.cn: 想两位徒步者站在山坡两侧，各看见一面。

abstract.en: See a camera lowered to a child’s height.
abstract.cn: 想镜头降到孩子的高度。

abstract.en: Hear a speaker say, from where I stand.
abstract.cn: 听人说我站的位置看到的是这样。

examples.en: The article presents the viewpoint of the workers, not the owners.
examples.cn: 这篇文章呈现的是工人的立场，而不是雇主的。

examples.en: Seen from a historical viewpoint, the treaty looks different.
examples.cn: 从历史的视角看，这份条约大不相同。

examples.en: The hilltop is the best viewpoint in the park.
examples.cn: 山顶是公园里最好的观景点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「唯一炮硬」——只有一门炮硬说有理，这就是他的观点。

root: view（看法，源自拉丁 videre「看」）+ point（点，源自拉丁 punctum）→ viewpoint

sensesIntro.en: A seeing plus a place gives a word that covers opinions, camera angles, and the hilltop where you stand to look.
sensesIntro.cn: 「看」加上「位置」，合成一个同时覆盖意见、机位与山顶观景处的词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people on opposite slopes of one hill.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一座山两侧的两个人。

branches.en: The farmer branch: a dam seen as a threat.
branches.cn: 农民分支：水坝被视为威胁。

branches.en: The hilltop branch: the best place to look down.
branches.cn: 山顶分支：俯瞰的最佳位置。

branches.en: The camera branch: a scene at a child’s height.
branches.cn: 镜头分支：孩子高度的场景。

branches.en: The debate branch: ten minutes for each side.
branches.cn: 辩论分支：每方十分钟。

branches.en: The evidence branch: five years of field data.
branches.cn: 证据分支：五年的实地数据。

intro.en: Viewpoint is built from two free words, view and point, each with its own Latin root.
intro.cn: viewpoint 由两个自由词 view 与 point 构成，各自有自己的拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: Videre, to see, supplies view; punctum, a dot, supplies point; English merely joints them.
latinIntro.cn: videre（看见）提供 view，punctum（点）提供 point，英语只是把二者拼合。

items.example: The second half fixes the place.
A viewpointed essay takes a clear side.
items.exampleCN: 有立场的文章总会偏向一方。

items.example: Standpoint is built the same way.
Perspective comes from per and specere.
items.exampleCN: perspective 来自 per 与 specere。

items.example: Outlook looks outward for a general view.
items.exampleCN: outlook 向外看，指总体看法。

definition_zh: 火炬；火把；手电筒；火种；（喻）指引
definition_en: a stick with burning material at one end, used as a light, or in American English a small electric light held in the hand
core_image: 夜里一支火把压得很低，火焰被风吹得偏向一侧
scene: 队伍沿着山路向上去看日出，最前面的人举着火把照路。 A guide with a torch led the way through the cave.
sceneCN: 这里 torch 是照明用的「火把/手电」（第 1 个义项：手持的照明器具）；句意为一名拿着火把的向导领着大家穿过洞穴。画面里有山路、洞口与前进的队伍。

pos.zh: 动词：（口语）故意纵火；烧毁

derivatives.zh: 加复数词尾 -es，义为「火把（复数）」
与 light 合成，义为「火光；手电光」
与 bearer 合成，义为「持火炬者；传承者」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「纵火；焚烧」

senses.title: A stick that burns as a light
senses.definition: a piece of wood or other material with a flame at one end, used to give light
senses.definitionCN: 一端燃着火焰的木棒或其他材料，用来照明
senses.example: The villagers walked to the shrine with torches in their hands.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们手持火把走向神庙。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the burning bundle itself, and everything else in English is drawn from it.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意义就是那束燃烧的东西本身，英语里的其余义项都从它引出。

senses.title: A small electric light
senses.definition: in British English, a small battery lamp carried in the hand
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中指手持的小型电池灯
senses.example: He took a torch from the drawer and went down to the cellar.
senses.exampleCN: 他从抽屉里拿出手电，下到地窖去了。
senses.why: British English keeps the old word for the new lamp, since both are portable hand-held lights.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语用旧的词指新的灯，因为两者都是手持的便携光源。

senses.title: A flame carried in relays
senses.definition: a symbolic flame carried from place to place, as at the Olympic games
senses.definitionCN: 在各地之间传递的象征性火焰，如奥运会火炬
senses.example: The torch was carried through the town by runners of all ages.
senses.exampleCN: 火炬由各年龄段的跑者传递穿过城镇。
senses.why: A relay flame is a torch that changes hands instead of going out, so the word becomes a symbol of continuity.
senses.whyCN: 接力的火焰是一支换了手却不熄灭的火把，于是这个词成了延续性的象征。

senses.title: The flame of a burning building
senses.definition: a fire set deliberately to destroy a building
senses.definitionCN: 为毁掉建筑而故意点燃的火
senses.example: The old mill was put to the torch during the unrest.
senses.exampleCN: 动乱中那座老磨坊被付之一炬。
senses.why: To put something to the torch is to give it up to the flame, a phrase that turns the light into a weapon.
senses.whyCN: 把某物交给火把，就是任其被焚，这个短语把光源变成了武器。

senses.title: A guide in the dark
senses.definition: something that gives light or understanding when all else is dark
senses.definitionCN: 在其余一切皆暗时给出光亮或理解的东西
senses.example: Her letters were a torch in the difficult winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那些信是艰难冬天里的一支火把。
senses.why: The image of the only light in a dark place makes the word natural for help and understanding.
senses.whyCN: 「暗处唯一的光」这一形象让这个词顺理成章地用于帮助与理解。

senses.title: A flame of devotion
senses.definition: used in the phrase carry a torch to mean holding an unreturned love
senses.definitionCN: 用于 carry a torch，表示怀有得不到回应的爱慕
senses.example: A flame that is kept burning inside and shown to no one is exactly the shape of a love not returned.
senses.exampleCN: 一簇在内里持续燃烧却不给任何人看的火，正是得不到回应的爱的形状。
senses.why: The phrase keeps the whole torch, flame and carrier together, because the lover is the one who holds the light.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把火把、火焰与持火者一并保留下来，因为爱慕者正是那个举着光的人。

senses.title: To set fire deliberately
senses.definition: in informal speech, to set fire to something on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指故意放火烧某物
senses.example: Someone torched the empty shed behind the school.
senses.exampleCN: 有人放火烧了学校后面那座空棚屋。
senses.why: The verb simply reverses the noun: what was a source of light becomes a means of destruction.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词只是把名词翻转：本来是光源的东西变成了毁灭的手段。

senses.title: A craft of flame in ritual
senses.definition: the burning light carried in processions and ceremonies
senses.definitionCN: 游行与仪式中被举着燃烧的光
senses.example: Each autumn the torch was lit at the top of the tower.
senses.exampleCN: 每年秋天，塔顶上的火把都会被点燃。
senses.why: Ritual keeps the oldest sense in full view: a flame that is carried, watched, and expected each year.
senses.whyCN: 仪式把最古老的意义完整保留：一簇每年被举着、被看着、被期待的火。

intro.en: Torch comes through Old French from Latin torqua or torca, a twisted thing, from the verb torquere, to twist, because a torch was a twist of fibre soaked in pitch.
intro.cn: torch 经古法语来自拉丁语 torqua 或 torca（绞成的东西），源于动词 torquere（扭、绞）；因为火把就是把纤维绞紧再浸上沥青。

items.en: Torquere means to twist or turn, and the derived noun names a twisted bundle.
items.cn: 拉丁语 torquere 意为扭、转，其派生名词指绞成的一束。

items.en: Torqua or torca names a twisted cord or a wreath, and the sense of a twisted firebrand develops from it.
items.cn: torqua 或 torca 指绞成的绳或花环，表示绞成之火炬的义项由此发展。

items.en: Old French torche is a twisted bundle of waxed or pitched fibre used as a light.
items.cn: 古法语 torche 指用蜡或沥青浸过的绞紧纤维束，用作照明。

items.en: English borrows torch in the thirteenth century for a portable light carried in the hand.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 torch，指可以手持携带的光源。

items.en: With the arrival of batteries the word is applied to a small electric lamp in British usage.
items.cn: 电池出现以后，英式用法把这个词用于小型电灯。

items.en: The figurative senses of passing the torch and carrying a torch are fixed in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: pass the torch 与 carry a torch 等比喻用法在十九至二十世纪定型。

note.en: The look-alike group collects other words built on the same twisting root, while the near-meaning group gathers kinds of light.
note.cn: 形近组收集建立在同一「扭绞」词根上的其他词，近义组则汇集各种光源。

entries.definition: the light given by a torch
the person who carries a torch
a covered area at the entrance of a building
entries.definitionCN: 门廊，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a light enclosed in a case
a stick of wax with a burning wick
the American word for a small electric torch
a fixed light that guides or warns

normalIntro.en: These memories use the twisted-bundle origin, the British and American split, and the idioms of carrying and passing.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用「绞紧的纤维束」这一来源、英美的词义分歧，以及挥舞与传递的习语。

normal.en: The Latin verb means to twist, so a torch is a twisted bundle before it is a light.
normal.cn: 那个拉丁动词意为扭，所以火把先是一束绞紧的东西，然后才是光源。

normal.en: In Britain a torch is a flashlight, which surprises many American readers.
normal.cn: 在英国 torch 就是手电筒，这常让美国读者意外。

normal.en: Pass the torch hands on a task or a tradition, as runners hand on a flame.
normal.cn: pass the torch 交接任务或传统，就像跑者传递火焰。

normal.en: Carry a torch for someone means loving without being loved back.
normal.cn: carry a torch for someone 意为单相思。

normal.en: Torque is the same root in engineering, a twisting force.
normal.cn: 工程上的 torque（扭矩）是同一词根，一种扭力。

abstract.en: Picture one small flame moving along a dark road, with ten people following it.
abstract.cn: 想象一小簇火焰沿暗路移动，十个人跟着它走。

abstract.en: Think of a hand cupped around a flame to keep the wind off.
abstract.cn: 想一只手掌围住火焰挡住风。

abstract.en: A torch is light that someone else is carrying for you, which is why it stands for guidance.
abstract.cn: 火把是别人替你举着的光，所以它能象征指引。

examples.en: The path was lit by torches fixed to the wall.
examples.cn: 小路被固定在墙上的火把照亮。

examples.en: She keeps a torch by the door in case of a power cut.
examples.cn: 她在门边放着一支手电，以防停电。

examples.en: The captain passed the torch to a younger officer.
examples.cn: 队长把接力棒（火种）交给了更年轻的军官。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「投掷」——把火把投掷出去照亮前路。

root: 拉丁语 torquere（扭、绞）→ torqua / torca（绞成之物）→ 古法语 torche → 英语 torch。同根词有 torque、torture；由「绞紧的纤维束」转为燃料光源。

sensesIntro.en: The entry begins with the burning stick, takes in the small electric lamp that inherited the name, then follows the flame into relays, rituals, arson, guidance, and longing.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从燃烧的木棒写起，收进继承了这个名字的小电灯，再顺着火焰走入接力、仪式、纵火、指引与思念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a twisted bundle burning at one end.
core.cn: 核心意象：一端燃烧的绞紧纤维束。

branches.en: The burning stick and the electric lamp.
branches.cn: 燃烧的木棒与电灯。

branches.en: The flame carried in relay and in ritual.
branches.cn: 在接力与仪式中被举着的火焰。

branches.en: Fire set to destroy, and the verb for it.
branches.cn: 用以毁灭的火及其动词。

branches.en: Light that guides or teaches.
branches.cn: 起指引或启迪作用的光。

branches.en: An unreturned love spoken of as a flame.
branches.cn: 被说成火焰的单方面爱慕。

intro.en: The word comes from a Latin twisting stem; English adds -es, -ed, and compounds with light and bearer.
intro.cn: 本词来自拉丁语表示「扭绞」的词干，英语加 -es、-ed，并与 light、bearer 构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the twisting verb and noun that lie behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的拉丁词条给出本词背后的「扭绞」动词与名词。

items.meaning: a twisted bundle used as a light
items.meaningCN: 绞紧的纤维束，用作光源
items.example: The stem comes into English whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干整体进入英语。

items.example: Torque and torture share the stem.
items.exampleCN: torque 与 torture 共用这个词干。

items.meaningCN: 用于 ch 之后的复数词尾

items.exampleCN: torching 出现在新闻报道中。

items.example: Torchlight is the light of a torch.
An electric torch is a flashlight.
items.exampleCN: an electric torch 就是手电筒。

items.example: The Olympic torch is the most famous one.
items.exampleCN: 奥运火炬是最著名的那一支。

latinEntries.meaning: a twisted engine of war; torture

definition_zh: 不重要的；无关紧要的；无足轻重的；微不足道的
definition_en: having little or no effect, value, or significance
core_image: 一堆文件里，最上面那张便签没人翻到过
scene: 会议开到一半，主持人在便签上写下的那条小字始终没人提起。 The detail seemed unimportant at the time.
sceneCN: 这里 unimportant 是「无关紧要的」（第 1 个义项：影响或价值极小）；句意为这个细节当时看起来无关紧要。没人翻到的便签正是这个词的核心。

pos.zh: 无足轻重的；微不足道的

collocations.zh: 认为某事不重要而不予理会

derivatives.zh: 形容词去掉 -ant 的名词形式，义为「不重要；无足轻重」
去掉否定前缀的形容词，义为「重要的」
肯定形式的名词，义为「重要性」
词族动词，义为「进口；意味」

senses.title: Having little effect
senses.definition: having little or no effect on what happens
senses.definitionCN: 对事情的发展几乎没有影响
senses.example: Whether the meeting starts ten minutes early is unimportant.
senses.exampleCN: 会议早开十分钟与否无关紧要。
senses.why: Import means to carry weight or meaning, so unimportant marks what carries none.
senses.whyCN: import 有「有分量、有意义」之义，因此 unimportant 标记那些毫无分量的东西。

senses.title: Small in value or status
senses.definition: having low rank or little standing among others
senses.definitionCN: 在他人之中地位低微、无足轻重
senses.example: He held an unimportant post in the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 他在部里担任一个无足轻重的职位。
senses.why: Weight in the mind becomes weight in the world, and lightness of weight means low standing.
senses.whyCN: 心中的分量会变成世上的分量，「无重量」便是地位低微。

senses.title: Too small to matter
senses.definition: used of a sum, a detail, or a fault too slight to matter
senses.definitionCN: 形容金额、细节或缺陷太小而无所谓
senses.example: They argued over a sum that was completely unimportant.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为一笔完全微不足道的款子争了起来。
senses.why: A thing that cannot tip the balance is unimportant, whichever scale is used.
senses.whyCN: 无论用哪杆秤，压不动天平的东西都不重要。

senses.title: Deliberately set aside
senses.definition: used when someone rates something as not worth attention
senses.definitionCN: 用于某人认定某事不值得关注时
senses.example: She swept the warning aside as unimportant.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那警告当作不重要而搁在一边。
senses.why: The word judges from a point of view, so it often reports how someone rates a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是从某个角度看问题，因此常用来转述某人如何评价一件事。

senses.title: Costing little attention or effort
senses.definition: used of tasks that need very little of one attention
senses.definitionCN: 形容只需要很少注意力的任务
senses.example: Filing is an unimportant job but it has to be done.
senses.exampleCN: 归档是件次要的活儿，但总得有人做。
senses.why: What carries no weight can also be carried with one hand, so it needs little effort.
senses.whyCN: 没有分量的东西一只手就能拿，所以也不费什么力气。

intro.en: Import came into English from Latin through French, and the negative adjective was formed in English.
intro.cn: import 经法语从拉丁语进入英语，否定形容词则是英语自己造的。

items.en: Importare meant to bring in, from in- and portare, to carry.
items.cn: importare 意为「带入」，由 in- 与 portare（搬运）构成。

items.en: Importer passed the verb into French with the sense of bringing in goods.
items.cn: importer 把动词带入法语，意为「运进货物」。

items.en: English borrowed import, which grew a sense of carrying meaning or weight.
items.cn: 英语借入 import，并衍生出「有含义、有分量」的意思。

items.en: The adjective important names what carries weight in the mind.
items.cn: 形容词 important 指在心中占有分量的东西。

items.en: Un- was prefixed to important to mark what carries none.
items.cn: 在 important 前加 un-，标记没有分量的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the import family, and the near-meaning group gathers words of smallness.
note.cn: 形近组是 import 词族，近义组汇集表示渺小的词。

normalIntro.en: The word denies carrying weight, and portare, to carry, is the hidden root.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词否定了「有分量」的搬运，而搬运的词根 portare 就藏在里面。

normal.en: Un- plus important: not carrying weight.
normal.cn: un- 加 important：无分量。

normal.en: Seem unimportant is the frame for a story that turns out badly.
normal.cn: seem unimportant 是那种事后出事的叙事的常用框架。

normal.en: Importance is the noun, and importantly is the sentence adverb.
normal.cn: importance 是名词，importantly 是句子副词。

normal.en: Import, transport, and portable share the carrying root portare.
normal.cn: import、transport 与 portable 共用「搬运」词根 portare。

normal.en: People often prefer not important to unimportant in speech.
normal.cn: 口语中人们常更愿意说 not important 而不是 unimportant。

abstract.en: Picture a sticky note on top of a file that nobody opens.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠文件上那张没人打开看的便签。

abstract.en: See a small name at the bottom of a long list.
abstract.cn: 看一长串名单末尾那个小名字。

abstract.en: Hear a warning that everyone nods at and forgets.
abstract.cn: 听一句人人点头忘却的警告。

examples.en: A detail that looked unimportant later solved the case.
examples.cn: 一个当时看似无关紧要的细节后来破了大案。

examples.en: Her role in the firm is not unimportant.
examples.cn: 她在公司里的角色并非无足轻重。

examples.en: They wasted an hour arguing about unimportant matters.
examples.cn: 他们为一个不重要的问题争论了一个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺 unimportant」——俺在这堆事里，就像纸角上那行小字，谁也不会多看一眼。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ important，important 由拉丁语 importare（带入）经法语 importer 演变而来，词根 portare 意为「搬运」

sensesIntro.en: The absence of weight explains why nothing here matters: no effect, no status, no size, no attention.
sensesIntro.cn: 缺少分量解释了这里为何一切都不重要：无影响、无地位、无体量、无需注意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small note that nobody ever turns to.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张始终没人翻到的便签。

branches.en: The effect branch: a detail that changes nothing.
branches.cn: 影响分支：改变不了任何事的细节。

branches.en: The status branch: a post of little standing.
branches.cn: 地位分支：地位低微的职位。

branches.en: The size branch: a sum too small to count.
branches.cn: 大小分支：小到不必计算的数额。

branches.en: The judgement branch: a person rating it low.
branches.cn: 评判分支：某人把它评为不重要。

branches.en: The effort branch: a task that asks little.
branches.cn: 用力分支：要求不高的任务。

intro.en: An English prefix on a French adjective built from a Latin verb of carrying.
intro.cn: 英语前缀压在一个法语形容词上，而它由拉丁语「搬运」动词构成。

latinIntro.en: Portare is the carrying root shared by import, transport, and export.
latinIntro.cn: portare 是「搬运」词根，import、transport、export 共用。

items.example: A trivial error cost them the match.
items.exampleCN: 一个小失误让他们输掉了比赛。

definition_en: a pleasant imagined situation, or a story built from imagination
core_image: 孩子躺在床上，闭眼想象自己骑着龙飞过城堡
scene: 她常常幻想自己住在海边。 She often has a fantasy about living by the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 fantasy 是「幻想」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她常幻想住在海边。

senses.title: Imagined situation
senses.definition: a pleasant situation that a person imagines but that is unlikely to happen
senses.definitionCN: 人想象出的愉快但不太可能发生的情境
senses.example: Winning the prize was only a fantasy.
senses.exampleCN: 获奖只是幻想。
senses.why: The core sense is a desired scene made in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是心中构建的愿望场景。

senses.title: Fantasy fiction
senses.definition: a story or genre full of magic and imaginary creatures
senses.definitionCN: 充满魔法与虚构生物的故事或文学类型
senses.example: She reads fantasy every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 她每晚读奇幻小说。
senses.why: A shared imagined world becomes a literary genre.
senses.whyCN: 共享的想象世界成为文学类型。

senses.title: Musical fantasy
senses.definition: a piece of music shaped freely by the composer's imagination
senses.definitionCN: 由作曲家想象自由构型的音乐作品
senses.example: The pianist played a fantasy by Mozart.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴家演奏了一首莫扎特幻想曲。
senses.why: Free imagination shapes music as it shapes stories.
senses.whyCN: 自由想象既塑造故事也塑造音乐。

intro.en: Fantasy comes from Greek phantasia, appearance or imagination.
intro.cn: fantasy 源自希腊语 phantasia（显现、想象）。

items.en: Phantasia meant a showing or an image in the mind.
items.cn: phantasia 意为显现或心中形象。

items.en: Phantasia meant imagination or a phantom.
items.cn: phantasia 意为想象或幻影。

items.en: Fantaisie meant imagination or a whim.
items.cn: fantaisie 意为想象或一时兴致。

items.en: Fantasy named the power of imagining.
items.cn: fantasy 指想象的能力。

items.en: Fantasy became a popular genre of fiction.
items.cn: fantasy 成为流行的文学类型。

note.en: Fantasy is compared with similar spellings and with words for imagination and dreams.
note.cn: 把 fantasy 与形近词以及表示想象和梦想的词作比较。

entries.definition: the power to form mental images

normalIntro.en: Fantasy is the full form behind fancy and fantastic.
normalIntro.cn: fantasy 是 fancy 与 fantastic 背后的完整形式。

normal.en: Fantasy is the long form; fancy is the short one.
normal.cn: fantasy 是长形式，fancy 是短形式。

normal.en: Fantasy novels build worlds with magic.
normal.cn: 奇幻小说用魔法构建世界。

normal.en: A fantasy is often a wish wearing a costume.
normal.cn: 幻想常是穿着戏服的愿望。

normal.en: Fantasize is the verb form with ize.
normal.cn: fantasize 是带 ize 的动词形式。

normal.en: The plural fantasies changes y to ies.
normal.cn: 复数 fantasies 要把 y 变成 ies。

abstract.en: Fantasy is where the mind tries on other lives.
abstract.cn: 幻想是心灵试穿他人生活的地方。

abstract.en: A shared fantasy can become a whole genre.
abstract.cn: 共享的幻想可以成为完整的文学类型。

abstract.en: Fantasy and reality need each other to be understood.
abstract.cn: 幻想与现实需要彼此才能被理解。

examples.en: He lives in a fantasy of wealth and fame.
examples.cn: 他活在名利双收的幻想中。

examples.en: The film is a fantasy set in a magic kingdom.
examples.cn: 这部电影是以魔法王国为背景的奇幻作品。

examples.en: Her childhood fantasy was to become an astronaut.
examples.cn: 她童年的幻想是成为宇航员。

dict_mnemonic.text: fantasy 是「幻想」的完整形式，fancy 是它的缩短版，fantastic 是「像幻想般奇妙」的形容词。

root: 源自希腊语 phantasia（显现、想象），核心义「在心中构建出的形象或情境」。

sensesIntro.en: Fantasy means an imagined situation, a genre of imaginative fiction, or a free musical piece.
sensesIntro.cn: fantasy 意为幻想情境、奇幻文学类型，或自由构型的幻想曲。

core.en: An imagined world built by the mind.
core.cn: 心灵构建的想象世界。

branches.en: A private imagined situation.
branches.cn: 私人的想象情境。

branches.en: An imagined world shared through fiction.
branches.cn: 通过小说共享的想象世界。

branches.en: Imagination shaping a musical piece.
branches.cn: 想象塑造的音乐作品。

branches.en: Private dreams and public stories both imagine worlds.
branches.cn: 私人梦想与公共故事都在想象世界。

branches.en: Both are creative forms built from imagination.
branches.cn: 两者都是由想象构建的创作形式。

intro.en: Fantasy has a family of verbs, writers, and adjectives.
intro.cn: fantasy 有动词、作家与形容词构成的词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek phantasia, imagination, is the distant root.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 phantasia（想象）是远源。

items.exampleCN: 这位奇幻作家发明了一个王国。

items.example: A fantastical castle rose above the trees.
items.exampleCN: 一座奇幻的城堡耸立在树梢之上。
这部奇幻小说卖得很好。

items.example: The game creates a fantasy world.
items.exampleCN: 游戏创造了一个幻想世界。

definition_en: a sudden large increase or forward movement
core_image: 海浪突然抬高，涌上堤岸
scene: 节日前电力需求猛增。 There was a surge in demand for electricity before the holiday.
sceneCN: 这里 surge 是「激增」（第 1 个义项）；句意：节日前电力需求猛增。

senses.title: A sudden increase
senses.definition: a sudden large increase in amount
senses.definitionCN: 数量突然大幅上升
senses.example: There was a surge in demand for electricity before the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 节日前电力需求猛增。
senses.why: This is the main modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的现代义项。

senses.title: A swelling rush
senses.definition: a strong forward movement of water or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 水或情绪的强烈涌动
senses.example: A surge of water hit the boat.
senses.exampleCN: 一股水流冲击着小船。
senses.why: Here the word is physical or emotional movement.
senses.whyCN: 这里指物理或情绪的涌动。

senses.title: To rise suddenly
senses.definition: to move forward or rise in a strong wave
senses.definitionCN: 以强烈的波浪向前或上升
senses.example: The crowd surged toward the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 人群向大门涌去。

senses.whyCN: 这是动词义项。

intro.en: Surge comes from Latin surgere, to rise.
intro.cn: surge 来自拉丁语 surgere，意为升起。

items.en: Sub meant from below.
items.cn: sub 意为从下面。

items.en: Regere meant to lead straight.
items.cn: regere 意为引导。

items.en: Surgere meant to rise up.
items.cn: surgere 意为升起。

items.en: Surge meant a rising wave.
items.cn: surge 意为上涨的波浪。

items.en: It came to mean a sudden increase.
items.cn: 它逐渐表示突然增加。

note.en: Surge is compared with look-alike words and with words for sudden increases.
note.cn: 把 surge 与形近词以及表示骤增的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: A surge is a wave that rises faster than expected.
normalIntro.cn: surge 是一道比预期涨得更快的浪。

normal.en: There was a surge in demand for electricity before the holiday.
normal.cn: 节日前电力需求猛增。

normal.en: A surge of water hit the boat.
normal.cn: 一股水流冲击着小船。

normal.en: The crowd surged toward the gate.
normal.cn: 人群向大门涌去。

normal.en: She felt a surge of anger.
normal.cn: 她感到一阵怒火。

normal.en: A power surge damaged the computer.
normal.cn: 电涌损坏了电脑。

abstract.en: A surge is a feeling that forgets the shore.
abstract.cn: 涌动，是一种忘了岸的情绪。

abstract.en: What rises fast may fall fast too.
abstract.cn: 涨得快的东西，也可能落得快。

abstract.en: Every wave is the sea practicing its voice.
abstract.cn: 每一道浪，都是海在练习自己的声音。

core.en: A force that rises and moves.
core.cn: 升起并向前移动的力量。

branches.en: The crowd surged toward the gate.
branches.cn: 人群向大门涌去。

branches.en: Numbers and waves can both surge.
branches.cn: 数字和波浪都可以涌动。

intro.en: Surge builds surging, upsurge, and resurgent.
intro.cn: surge 可构成 surging、upsurge 和 resurgent。

latinIntro.cn: 这个词根是拉丁语 surgere，意为升起。

The city saw a cultural resurgence.
