definition_en: to bend the body forward and down, to lower oneself, or a small porch
core_image: 一个人弓着背俯身拾起地上的东西
scene: 他弯腰捡起钥匙。 He stooped to pick up the key.
sceneCN: 这里 stoop 是「弯腰」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他弯腰捡起钥匙。

senses.title: Bend down
senses.definition: to bend the body forward and down
senses.definitionCN: 身体向前下方弯曲
senses.example: He stooped to pick up the key.
senses.exampleCN: 他弯腰捡起钥匙。
senses.why: This is the basic bodily action.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的身体动作。

senses.title: Lower oneself
senses.definition: to lower oneself to do something wrong or unworthy
senses.definitionCN: 自降身份去做错误或不体面的事
senses.example: She would never stoop to lying.
senses.exampleCN: 她绝不会堕落到撒谎。
senses.why: Bending the body becomes bending one's standards.
senses.whyCN: 弯下身体，引申为降低标准。

senses.title: A small porch
senses.definition: a small porch with steps at the entrance of a house
senses.definitionCN: 房屋入口带台阶的小门廊
senses.example: They sat on the stoop and talked.
senses.exampleCN: 他们坐在门前台阶上聊天。
senses.why: The place where one steps down takes the name.
senses.whyCN: 人走下的那处台阶沿用了这个词。

intro.en: Stoop comes from an Old English verb for bowing.
intro.cn: stoop 来自一个表示低头的古英语动词。

items.en: The root meant to bow or bend.
items.cn: 该词根意为低头或弯曲。

items.en: Old English stupian meant to bow down.
items.cn: 古英语 stupian 意为俯身低头。

items.en: Stoop named the bent posture.
items.cn: stoop 指弯腰的姿势。

items.en: Stoop to meant to lower oneself.
items.cn: stoop to 表示自降身份。

items.en: Stoop named a porch in American English.
items.cn: stoop 在美式英语中指门廊。

note.en: Stoop is compared with look-alike words and with words for bending.
note.cn: 把 stoop 与形近词以及表示弯曲的词作比较。

entries.definition: to bend the head or body

normalIntro.en: To stoop is to bring your head nearer the ground.
normalIntro.cn: stoop 就是把头靠近地面。

normal.en: He stooped to tie his shoe.
normal.cn: 他弯腰系鞋带。

normal.en: Do not stoop for long.
normal.cn: 不要长时间弯腰。

normal.en: She stooped over the baby.
normal.cn: 她俯身看着婴儿。

normal.en: He would not stoop to cheat.
normal.cn: 他不肯堕落到作弊。

normal.en: They sat on the stoop at dusk.
normal.cn: 黄昏时他们坐在门前台阶上。

abstract.en: Stooping to lift another is not a loss of height.
abstract.cn: 弯腰去扶别人，并不算矮了一截。

abstract.en: Some people stoop only to pick up what they dropped.
abstract.cn: 有些人弯腰，只是为了捡回自己丢掉的东西。

abstract.en: A bent back can still carry a straight heart.
abstract.cn: 弯下的背，仍能扛着一颗挺直的心。

examples.en: He stooped to pick up the key.
examples.cn: 他弯腰捡起钥匙。

examples.en: She would never stoop to lying.
examples.cn: 她绝不会堕落到撒谎。

examples.en: They sat on the stoop and talked.
examples.cn: 他们坐在门前台阶上聊天。

dict_mnemonic.text: stoop 是「弯腰」，stoop to 是屈尊或堕落到做某事；名词 stoop 在美式英语里指门前的台阶与门廊。

root: 来自古英语 stupian（俯身低头），与日耳曼语同源；由身体的下弯，引申为身份与品格的降低，名词又指人进出门时走上走下的台阶门廊。

sensesIntro.en: Stoop is to bend down, to lower oneself, or a small entrance porch.
sensesIntro.cn: stoop 是弯腰、自降身份，或入口处的小门廊。

core.en: A body folded toward the ground.
core.cn: 一具朝地面折下的身体。

branches.en: He stooped to pick up the key.
branches.cn: 他弯腰捡起钥匙。

branches.en: She would never stoop to lying.
branches.cn: 她绝不会堕落到撒谎。

branches.en: They sat on the stoop and talked.
branches.cn: 他们坐在门前台阶上聊天。

branches.en: The body bends, and so do standards.
branches.cn: 身体弯下去，标准也跟着弯。

branches.en: The porch is where you stoop to enter.
branches.cn: 门廊，正是你低头进门的地方。

intro.en: Stoop takes endings and builds phrases of bending.
intro.cn: stoop 加词尾，并构成表示弯腰的短语。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: She stooped to tie her shoe.
He walked with a stooping back.
He would not stoop to cheat.
They sat on the front stoop.

definition_zh: 老兵；退伍军人；老手；（美）经验丰富的人
definition_en: a person who has served in the armed forces, or who has long experience in a field
core_image: 一位老兵胸前挂满勋章站在队列最前面
scene: 纪念日游行上，一位老兵被请到最前面，人群为他鼓掌。 A veteran of the war led the parade with a slow, steady step.
sceneCN: 这里 veteran 是「老兵」（第 1 个义项：在军队中服役过的人）；句意为一位老兵迈着缓慢而稳的步子领着游行队伍。胸前挂满勋章的那个人就是这个词的形象。

collocations.zh: 经历过两次战争的老兵

derivatives.zh: 由 veteran 加 -ship 构成，义为「老兵身份；老练」
同源词，来自 veterinarius（管牲口的人），义为「兽医的」
加前缀 in- 构成，义为「积习难改的；根深蒂固的」

senses.title: A soldier who has served for long
senses.definition: someone who has served a long time in the armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 在军队中长期服役或曾经服役的人
senses.example: A veteran of the war led the parade with a slow, steady step.
senses.exampleCN: 一位战争老兵迈着缓慢而稳的步子领着游行队伍。
senses.why: Latin veteranus was the word for an old soldier, and that is still the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 veteranus 本来就是「老士兵」，这至今仍是首要义项。

senses.title: Someone with deep experience
senses.definition: a person who has a lot of experience in a job or activity
senses.definitionCN: 在工作或活动中经验丰富的人
senses.example: She is a veteran of three national campaigns.
senses.exampleCN: 她是三次全国性竞选的老手。
senses.why: Old soldiers were valued for their years in the field, and the same word was lent to other fields.
senses.whyCN: 老兵的可靠来自多年的战场经验，这个词随后被借到别的领域。

senses.title: A vehicle or article long in use
senses.definition: a thing that has been used a long time and done good service
senses.definitionCN: 使用多年、立过功的旧车或旧物
senses.example: He still drives his veteran car on weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 周末他仍开着自己那辆老牌车。
senses.why: The idea of long service applies to machines as to people.
senses.whyCN: 「服役多年」的想法既可以用于人，也可以用于机器。

senses.title: The adjective for long-tested skill
senses.definition: having long experience and therefore being reliable
senses.definitionCN: 有长久经验因而可靠的
senses.example: A veteran teacher knows which question to ask first.
senses.exampleCN: 经验丰富的老师知道先问哪个问题。
senses.why: Once a noun of experience, the word can sit before another noun as a badge of reliability.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦表示经验，就可以放在别的名词前，作为可靠的标记。

senses.title: A former serviceman recognised by the state
senses.definition: a former member of the forces entitled to state support
senses.definitionCN: 依法享有国家优待的退役军人
senses.example: The clinic offers free care for veterans.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为退伍军人提供免费治疗。
senses.why: Once service ends, the word turns into an official label with rights attached.
senses.whyCN: 服役结束之后，这个词又变成附带权利的官方身份。

intro.en: Veteran came straight from Latin veteranus, an old soldier, from vetus, old.
intro.cn: veteran 直接来自拉丁语 veteranus（老士兵），源于 vetus（老的）。

items.en: Vetus meant old, and veteranus named an old soldier.
items.cn: vetus 意为老的，veteranus 指老士兵。

items.en: Roman writers also used vetera for things long in use.
items.cn: 罗马作家也用 vetera 指使用很久的东西。

items.en: English adopted veteran in the sixteenth century for long-serving soldiers.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪引入 veteran，指服役已久的军人。

items.en: Through the nineteenth century it spread to any long-tested worker.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，它扩展到任何久经考验的从业者。

items.en: The adjective uses now include veteran services and veteran cars.
items.cn: 如今形容词用法包括退伍军人服务和老牌老爷车。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same stem, the second the close words for an experienced person.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干的词，第二组是表示有经验者的相近词。

entries.definition: long established and hard to change
an old car kept in good order

normalIntro.en: Latin vetus, old, is the whole secret: a veteran is simply someone who has been around a long time.
normalIntro.cn: 全部秘密就在拉丁语 vetus（老的）：veteran 就是待得够久的人。

normal.en: Veteran, veterinary, and inveterate all rest on Latin vetus, old.
normal.cn: veteran、veterinary、inveterate 都建立在拉丁语 vetus（老的）之上。

normal.en: Picture the oldest head in the line, wearing the most medals.
normal.cn: 想队列中最年长的那颗头，挂的勋章最多。

normal.en: The word moved from soldiers to any long-serving worker.
normal.cn: 这个词从士兵扩展到任何长期从业的人。

normal.en: The plural is plain veterans, no doubling.
normal.cn: 复数是直接的 veterans，不双写辅音。

normal.en: Before another noun it becomes an adjective: veteran teacher.
normal.cn: 放在另一个名词前就作形容词：veteran teacher。

abstract.en: See one slow, steady step leading a whole parade.
abstract.cn: 想一个缓慢而稳的步子带着整支队伍前进。

abstract.en: Think of an old coat that has lasted through many winters.
abstract.cn: 想一件熬过许多个冬天的旧大衣。

abstract.en: Hear medals click softly against each other as he walks.
abstract.cn: 听勋章随着脚步轻轻相碰。

examples.en: My grandfather is a veteran who served for twenty years.
examples.cn: 我祖父是一位服役二十年的老兵。

examples.en: She is a veteran of the newspaper world.
examples.cn: 她是报界的老手。

examples.en: Veteran staff were asked to train the newcomers.
examples.cn: 资深员工被安排去培训新人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维特伦」——老魏特守在队伍最前面，是个老兵。

root: 拉丁语 vetus（老的）→ veteranus（老士兵）→ 法语 vétéran → 英语 veteran

sensesIntro.en: A Latin word for old grows from long service in the army, to skill in any trade, to old machines and official standing.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个拉丁语中表示「老」的词，从军队里的长期服役，长到各行各业的熟练，再长到旧机器与官方身份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old soldier leading a parade.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位老兵领着游行队伍。

branches.en: The army branch: a soldier of the old war.
branches.cn: 军队分支：上一场战争的老兵。

branches.en: The career branch: veteran of three campaigns.
branches.cn: 职业分支：三次竞选的老手。

branches.en: The machine branch: the old car driven on Sundays.
branches.cn: 机器分支：周末才开的老牌车。

branches.en: The adjective branch: the veteran teacher who knows what to ask.
branches.cn: 形容词分支：知道先问什么的资深教师。

branches.en: The rights branch: free care for veterans.
branches.cn: 权利分支：为退伍军人提供免费医疗。

intro.en: The stem veter- carries old, and endings such as -an and -ship build the family.
intro.cn: 词干 veter- 携带「老」的含义，-an、-ship 等后缀构成这个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vetus gave veteranus, and English also borrowed veterinarian and the prefix in- form inveterate from the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vetus 派生 veteranus，英语还从同一词干借来 veterinarian 与带前缀的 inveterate。

items.example: Veter- holds the sense of long use.
items.exampleCN: veter- 携带「经久使用」之义。

items.example: A veteran was a person grown old in war.
items.exampleCN: veteran 原指在战争中变老的人。

items.example: Veteranship names the standing of a veteran.
Veterinary medicine deals with old and sick animals.
items.exampleCN: veterinary 医学处理的是老龄与生病的动物。

items.example: Inveterate means settled in by age.
items.exampleCN: inveterate 意为因年久而固定下来。

items.example: Recruits arrive while veterans stand guard.
items.exampleCN: 新兵到来时老兵在站岗。

items.example: A novice learns what a veteran knows.
items.exampleCN: 新手正在学习老兵已懂的东西。

items.example: An expert and a veteran are often the same person.
Veterans Day is marked in November.

definition_en: to take hold of something firmly, or to understand it
core_image: 一只手紧紧握住门把
scene: 他抓住绳子，爬上了岸。 He grasped the rope and climbed ashore.
sceneCN: 这里 grasp 是「抓住」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他抓住绳子，爬上了岸。

senses.title: Hold firmly
senses.definition: to take hold of something firmly
senses.definitionCN: 紧紧地握住某物
senses.example: He grasped the rope and climbed ashore.
senses.exampleCN: 他抓住绳子，爬上了岸。
senses.why: The physical grip is the core sense.
senses.whyCN: 身体上的抓握，是这个词的核心。

senses.title: Understand
senses.definition: to understand something fully
senses.definitionCN: 完全理解某事
senses.example: She quickly grasped the main idea.
senses.exampleCN: 她很快领会了要点。
senses.why: The mind is pictured as taking hold of an idea.
senses.whyCN: 把心智领会概念比作用手抓住。

senses.title: Reach or understanding
senses.definition: the ability to reach or understand something
senses.definitionCN: 触及或理解某事的能力
senses.example: The task is within his grasp.
senses.exampleCN: 这项任务在他能力范围之内。
senses.why: The noun names the limit of hand and mind.
senses.whyCN: 名词义指手与心智所能触及的界限。

intro.en: Grasp appears in Middle English as a word for feeling with the hand.
intro.cn: grasp 在中古英语中出现，指用手摸索。

items.en: The word appears in Middle English as graspen.
items.cn: 这个词在中古英语中作 graspen。

items.en: Graspen meant to feel or grope for.
items.cn: graspen 意为摸索、探寻。

items.en: It narrowed to taking hold with the hand.
items.cn: 词义缩小为用手抓住。

items.en: The mental sense of understanding developed.
items.cn: 发展出「理解」的心理义。

items.en: The noun named reach and control.
items.cn: 名词义指触及范围与掌控。

note.en: Grasp is compared with look-alike words and words for holding.
note.cn: 把 grasp 与形近词以及表示抓握的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Grasp is the hand closing, then the mind opening.
normalIntro.cn: grasp 是手合上，然后心智打开。

normal.en: Grasp the handle tightly.
normal.cn: 紧紧握住把手。

normal.en: She grasped my hand.
normal.cn: 她抓住了我的手。

normal.en: I finally grasped the rule.
normal.cn: 我终于弄懂了这个规则。

normal.en: He grasped the chance to study.
normal.cn: 他抓住了学习的机会。

normal.en: Victory is within our grasp.
normal.cn: 胜利就在我们掌握之中。

abstract.en: Some things are held by the hand, some by the mind.
abstract.cn: 有些东西用手握，有些用心握。

abstract.en: A chance slips past an open hand.
abstract.cn: 机会会从张开的手边滑过。

abstract.en: To grasp is to make the distant near.
abstract.cn: 抓住，就是把远的拉近。

examples.en: He grasped the rope and climbed ashore.
examples.cn: 他抓住绳子，爬上了岸。

examples.en: She quickly grasped the main idea.
examples.cn: 她很快领会了要点。

examples.en: The task is within his grasp.
examples.cn: 这项任务在他能力范围之内。

dict_mnemonic.text: grasp 既是「抓住」，也是「领会」；grasp a chance 是抓住机会，within one's grasp 是力所能及；注意与 grass（草）、graph（图表）区分。

root: 中古英语 graspen 意为摸索、抓取，词源不详；核心义由手部的抓握扩展到心智的领会与能力的范围。

sensesIntro.en: Grasp means to hold firmly, to understand, or the reach of hand and mind.
sensesIntro.cn: grasp 指紧握、理解，或手与心智所能触及的范围。

core.en: The hand closes on something, then the mind does.
core.cn: 手先握住某物，接着心也握住。

branches.en: Fingers lock around a rope.
branches.cn: 手指扣住绳子。

branches.en: A rule clicks into place.
branches.cn: 一条规则忽然想通了。

branches.en: A goal sits just inside reach.
branches.cn: 目标就在伸手可及的范围内。

branches.en: Hand and mind use the same grip.
branches.cn: 手与心，用的是同一种握法。

branches.en: What is understood is also controlled.
branches.cn: 理解了的东西，也被掌握了。

intro.en: Grasp forms verb parts and adjectives.
intro.cn: grasp 构成动词变化和形容词。

latinIntro.en: Grasp has no Latin root; its origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: grasp 没有拉丁词根，其词源不详。

items.example: She grasps the idea at once.
items.exampleCN: 她立刻就领会了这个想法。
那个贪婪的人想要更多。

items.example: The child is a quick grasper.
He looked at the gold graspingly.

items.exampleCN: 这个规模令人无法想象。

definition_en: a round solid shape, an area of activity, or a group within society
core_image: 地球仪在灯下缓缓转动，蓝色球面上映出窗外的光
scene: 地球仪是一个代表地球的球体。 A globe is a sphere that represents the earth.
sceneCN: 这里 sphere 是「球体」（第 1 个义项）；句意：地球仪是一个代表地球的球体。

senses.title: A round solid
senses.definition: a perfectly round solid shape like a ball
senses.definitionCN: 像球一样完全圆形的立体形状
senses.example: A globe is a sphere that represents the earth.
senses.exampleCN: 地球仪是一个代表地球的球体。
senses.why: This is the geometric sense at the root of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词根源处的几何含义。

senses.title: An area of activity
senses.definition: a particular area of activity or knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 活动或知识的某一特定范围
senses.example: She works in the sphere of education.
senses.exampleCN: 她在教育领域工作。
senses.why: A sphere encloses a space, and so does an area of work.
senses.whyCN: 球体围出一片空间，工作领域也是如此。

senses.title: A social circle
senses.definition: a group of people with shared interests or position
senses.definitionCN: 兴趣或地位相同的一群人
senses.example: He moved in a different social sphere.
senses.exampleCN: 他进入了另一个社交圈子。
senses.why: A social circle is a sphere drawn around people.
senses.whyCN: 社交圈就是围绕人们画出的一个球。

intro.en: Sphere came from Greek sphaira, a ball, through Latin.
intro.cn: sphere 从希腊语 sphaira（球）经拉丁语而来。

items.en: Sphaira meant a ball or a globe.
items.cn: sphaira 意为球或球体。

items.en: Sphaera named a globe and the heavens.
items.cn: sphaera 指球体与天球。

items.en: Sphere entered English as the shape of the heavens.
items.cn: sphere 以天球的形状之义进入英语。

items.en: It named the earth and other round bodies.
items.cn: 它指地球等圆形天体。

items.en: It came to mean a field of activity or influence.
items.cn: 它逐渐表示活动或影响力的范围。

note.en: Sphere is compared with look-alike words and words for round shapes and fields.
note.cn: 把 sphere 与形近词以及表示圆形和领域的词作比较。

entries.definition: a round model of the earth
an area of study or work

normalIntro.en: A sphere is a space drawn into a perfect round, then borrowed for any enclosed area.
normalIntro.cn: sphere 是一片被画成完美圆形的空间，随后借指任何被围起来的范围。

normal.en: A globe is a sphere that represents the earth.
normal.cn: 地球仪是一个代表地球的球体。

normal.en: She works in the sphere of education.
normal.cn: 她在教育领域工作。

normal.en: He moved in a different social sphere.
normal.cn: 他进入了另一个社交圈子。

normal.en: The moon appears as a pale sphere.
normal.cn: 月亮看上去是一个苍白的球体。

normal.en: Each country guards its sphere of influence.
normal.cn: 每个国家都守护自己的势力范围。

abstract.en: A sphere is a wall that has no corners.
abstract.cn: 球体是一堵没有角落的墙。

abstract.en: Every field is a sphere someone drew around an interest.
abstract.cn: 每个领域都是某人围绕兴趣画出的球。

abstract.en: The wider your sphere, the more edges you meet.
abstract.cn: 圈子越大，你碰到的边界越多。

examples.en: A globe is a sphere that represents the earth.
examples.cn: 地球仪是一个代表地球的球体。

examples.en: She works in the sphere of education.
examples.cn: 她在教育领域工作。

examples.en: He moved in a different social sphere.
examples.cn: 他进入了另一个社交圈子。

dict_mnemonic.text: sphere 源自希腊语 sphaira（球），指「球体」，引申为「范围、领域、圈子」；spherical 是「球形的」，hemisphere 是「半球」，sphere of influence 是「势力范围」。

root: 来自希腊语 sphaira（球），经拉丁语 sphaera 进入英语，核心义为球体，引申为像球一样围出的范围、领域与社交圈。

sensesIntro.en: Sphere means a round solid, an area of activity, or a social circle.
sensesIntro.cn: sphere 指球体、活动领域，或社交圈子。

core.en: A space enclosed in a perfect round.
core.cn: 被完美圆形围起的空间。

branches.en: A globe turns under a lamp.
branches.cn: 地球仪在灯下转动。

branches.en: A teacher works inside one branch of knowledge.
branches.cn: 一位教师在某一知识分支内工作。

branches.en: Guests gather in a small circle of friends.
branches.cn: 宾客聚成一个小小的朋友圈。

branches.en: A round boundary and a bounded field share one shape.
branches.cn: 圆形边界与有界的领域共享一种形状。

branches.en: Work and society each draw their own circles.
branches.cn: 工作与社会各自画出自己的圆圈。

intro.en: Sphere forms adjectives and compound worlds.
intro.cn: sphere 构成形容词和表示各种圈层的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek sphaira through Latin sphaera, a ball.
latinIntro.cn: 其词根是希腊语 sphaira，经拉丁语 sphaera（球）而来。

items.example: A globe is a sphere that represents the earth.
items.exampleCN: 地球仪是一个代表地球的球体。

items.example: The lamps hung like small spheres.

items.exampleCN: 这些种子几乎是球形的。

items.example: The northern hemisphere is colder now.

items.exampleCN: 大气层保护着这颗行星。

items.meaning: the living zone of the earth

items.example: The balloon rose into the stratosphere.

definition_en: a person or thing used in place of another, or to use one in place of another
core_image: 场上有人下场，另一个人穿上同一位置的球衣
scene: 没有蜂蜜时，可以用糖代替。 You can substitute sugar for honey.
sceneCN: 这里 substitute 是「代替」（第 1 个义项）；句意：没有蜂蜜时，可以用糖代替。

senses.title: Use instead
senses.definition: to use one thing or person in place of another
senses.definitionCN: 用一物或一人取代另一物或另一人
senses.example: You can substitute sugar for honey.
senses.exampleCN: 没有蜂蜜时，可以用糖代替。
senses.why: This is the basic verb sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的动词义项。

senses.title: Replacement
senses.definition: a thing used instead of another
senses.definitionCN: 用来取代另一物的东西
senses.example: There is no substitute for clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 干净的水无可替代。
senses.why: The verb becomes a noun for the stand-in.
senses.whyCN: 动词转成名词，指替代的东西。

senses.title: Reserve player
senses.definition: a player who replaces another in a game
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中替换上场的球员
senses.example: The substitute scored in the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 替补球员在最后一分钟进球。
senses.why: Sport gives the word a person sense.
senses.whyCN: 体育赋予这个词指人的用法。

intro.en: Substitute comes from Latin for setting one thing under another.
intro.cn: substitute 来自拉丁语，意为把一物放到另一物的位置上。

items.en: Sub meant under or in place of.
items.cn: sub 意为在下或代替。

items.en: Statuere meant to set or place.
items.cn: statuere 意为放置。

items.en: Substituere meant to put in place of another.
items.cn: substituere 意为放到另一物的位置。

items.en: Substitute named a person or thing used instead.
items.cn: substitute 指被用来替代的人或物。

items.en: Substitute became common in sport and teaching.
items.cn: substitute 在体育和教学中变得常见。

note.en: Substitute is compared with look-alike words and with words for replacement.
note.cn: 把 substitute 与形近词以及表示替代的词作比较。

entries.definition: to put something new in place of another
a thing that takes another's place

normalIntro.en: A substitute stands in the same place as the original.
normalIntro.cn: substitute 站到原本那个东西的位置上。

normal.en: You can substitute sugar for honey.
normal.cn: 没有蜂蜜时，可以用糖代替。

normal.en: There is no substitute for clean water.
normal.cn: 干净的水无可替代。

normal.en: The substitute scored in the last minute.
normal.cn: 替补球员在最后一分钟进球。

normal.en: She substituted for the sick teacher.
normal.cn: 她给生病的老师代课。

normal.en: They used oil as a substitute for butter.
normal.cn: 他们用油代替黄油。

abstract.en: A substitute can fill a seat but not a memory.
abstract.cn: 替代品能占住位子，却填不满记忆。

abstract.en: Every substitute carries the shadow of what it replaces.
abstract.cn: 每个替代品，都带着被替代者的影子。

abstract.en: Some things have no substitute, only a next best.
abstract.cn: 有些东西没有替代品，只有次好的选择。

examples.en: You can substitute sugar for honey.
examples.cn: 没有蜂蜜时，可以用糖代替。

examples.en: There is no substitute for clean water.
examples.cn: 干净的水无可替代。

examples.en: She substituted for the sick teacher.
examples.cn: 她给生病的老师代课。

dict_mnemonic.text: substitute 是「代替」，也可作名词指「替代品、替补」；substitute for 是代替，no substitute for 是无可替代，a substitute teacher 是代课老师。

root: 来自拉丁语 substituere，由 sub（在下、代替）与 statuere（放置）组合，字面是「放到另一个的位置上」；因此表示代替、替换，也指替代的人或物。

sensesIntro.en: Substitute means to use in place of another, the replacement itself, or a reserve player.
sensesIntro.cn: substitute 表示代替、替代品，或替补球员。

core.en: One thing standing in the place of another.
core.cn: 一个东西站到另一个东西的位置上。

branches.en: You can substitute sugar for honey.
branches.cn: 没有蜂蜜时，可以用糖代替。

branches.en: There is no substitute for clean water.
branches.cn: 干净的水无可替代。

branches.en: The substitute scored in the last minute.
branches.cn: 替补球员在最后一分钟进球。

branches.en: The act of replacing and the replacement share one word.
branches.cn: 替换的动作和替换物共用一个词。

branches.en: A thing and a player can both be substitutes.
branches.cn: 一件东西和一名球员，都可以是替补。

intro.en: Substitute takes -ion and -able to build its family.
intro.cn: substitute 借助 -ion 和 -able 构成同族词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base stitu- meant set or placed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 stitu- 意为放置。

items.example: He is substituting for the manager.
A substitute teacher took the class.

latinEntries.meaning: to put in place of another
latinEntries.exampleCN: substituere 演变为英语的 substitute。

definition_zh: 透明的；清澈的；易懂的；公开的
definition_en: clear enough to see through, easy to understand, or open for everyone to see
core_image: 清晨的窗玻璃干净得像不存在，树枝的影子直接落在桌面
scene: 雪后的早晨，窗玻璃擦得发亮，外面的鸟落在枝上。 The lake was so transparent that we saw stones on the bottom.
sceneCN: 这里 transparent 是「透明的；清澈的」（第 1 个义项：能看清后面东西的）；句意为湖水清澈得能看见水底的石头。擦得很亮的窗和清得见底的水，都是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 transparent 加 -cy 构成，义为「透明；透明度」
由 transparent 加 -ly 构成，义为「透明地；显然地」
由 semi-（半）与 transparent 复合，义为「半透明的」

senses.title: Seeing straight through
senses.definition: clear enough for light to pass through, so objects behind can be seen
senses.definitionCN: 足够清澈让光线通过，因而能看见后面的物体
senses.example: The lake was so transparent that we saw stones on the bottom.
senses.exampleCN: 湖水清澈得能看见水底的石头。
senses.why: Latin trans, through, plus parere, to appear, means letting light appear through the body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 trans（穿过）加 parere（显现），意为让光穿过物体显现出来。

senses.title: Water you can look into
senses.definition: used of water that is free of mud or cloudiness
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容水中没有泥沙或浑浊物
senses.example: Children watched the transparent stream flow over the pebbles.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们看着清澈的小溪流过卵石。
senses.why: Clear water is the everyday picture of the whole idea, so the adjective drifted into it naturally.
senses.whyCN: 清水是这一概念的日常画面，形容词自然就延伸到了这里。

senses.title: Easy to follow
senses.definition: expressed so simply that nobody can misunderstand it
senses.definitionCN: 表达得简单明了，不会被误解
senses.example: Her explanation was transparent even to the beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 即使是初学者也能听懂她的解释。
senses.why: If nothing hides the meaning, the words are transparent in the same way glass is.
senses.whyCN: 如果没有任何东西遮住含义，那么这些词就像玻璃一样透明。

senses.title: Open to inspection
senses.definition: used of rules or actions that anyone may examine and judge
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容任何人可以查看与评判的规则或行为
senses.example: The committee promised a transparent selection process.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会承诺采用公开透明的选拔流程。
senses.why: Modern politics borrowed the glass image for institutions that have nothing to hide.
senses.whyCN: 现代政治借用了玻璃的意象，形容没什么可隐藏的机构。

intro.en: Transparent comes from the Latin verb transparere, to show through, made of trans, through, and parere, to appear.
intro.cn: transparent 来自拉丁语动词 transparere（透出），由 trans（穿过）与 parere（显现）组成。

items.en: Parere meant to come into sight or be visible, the root of appear.
items.cn: parere 意为出现、可见，是 appear 的词根。

items.en: Transparens described bodies that let light pass and show what lies behind.
items.cn: transparens 形容能让光透过、显出背后事物的物体。

items.en: French borrowed it in the sense of showing light through a material.
items.cn: 法语借入时指让光透过材料显现出来。

items.en: English extended the adjective from glass and water to arguments and excuses.
items.cn: 英语把这个形容词从玻璃和水扩展到论证与借口。

items.en: Public life adopted the word for open government and honest rules.
items.cn: 公共生活借用它来指开放的政府与诚实的规则。

note.en: The first group shares the par, to appear, stem, the second holds other words about clarity.
note.cn: 第一组共享 par（显现）词干，第二组收其他表示清晰的词。

entries.definition: The quality of being clear or open.
In a clear and open way.
Easy to see through or understand.
Letting light through without showing shapes clearly.
So thin or clear that shapes show through.

normalIntro.en: Transparent can be read as trans plus parent: something you can see straight through to the others behind it.
normalIntro.cn: transparent 可以读成 trans 加 parent：你能一眼看穿它，看到后面的东西。

normal.en: Par is the appear root of apparent and appear.
normal.cn: par 是 apparent 与 appear 里表示「显现」的词根。

normal.en: Trans moves across, so light moves straight through.
normal.cn: trans 是穿过，于是光笔直透过去。

normal.en: The noun ends in -cy: transparency.
normal.cn: 名词以 -cy 结尾：transparency。

normal.en: Stress falls on the second syllable: transPARent.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：transPARent。

normal.en: A transparent excuse is one that hides nothing, including the truth.
normal.cn: transparent excuse 是不藏东西的借口，包括不藏真相。

abstract.en: A window so clean that the tree seems to stand indoors.
abstract.cn: 窗户干净得树仿佛长在屋里。

abstract.en: A glass of water on white paper, almost invisible.
abstract.cn: 白纸上一杯几乎看不见的水。

abstract.en: A sentence that lets the meaning through without a shadow.
abstract.cn: 一句让意思毫无阴影地穿过的话。

examples.en: The lid is transparent, so you can watch the seeds grow.
examples.cn: 盖子透明，所以你能看到种子发芽。

examples.en: The river runs transparent over smooth grey stones.
examples.cn: 河水清澈地流过光滑的灰石。

examples.en: Their rules of choosing members are written in a transparent way.
examples.cn: 他们选择成员的规则写得清楚透明。

dict_mnemonic.text: trans（穿过）＋ parent（显现）——光穿过它还能显出后面，就是透明的。

root: 拉丁语 transparere（透出），trans（穿过）＋parere（显现、出现），词干 par- 也见于 apparent、appear；同族词有 transparency、transparently。

sensesIntro.en: Glass first, then clear water, then clear words, then open institutions.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是玻璃，再是清水，然后是明白的话语，最后是公开的机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a window so clean it almost vanishes.
core.cn: 核心意象：干净得几乎消失的窗。

branches.en: The glass branch: light passes and objects appear.
branches.cn: 玻璃分支：光穿过，物体显现。

branches.en: The water branch: nothing cloudy blocks the view.
branches.cn: 水分支：没有浑物挡住视线。

branches.en: The language branch: meaning shows through the words.
branches.cn: 语言分支：意思透过词显现。

branches.en: The institution branch: nothing is kept out of sight.
branches.cn: 机构分支：没有东西被藏起来。

branches.en: The image branch: glass and sentences share one picture.
branches.cn: 意象分支：玻璃与句子共用同一幅画。

intro.en: Transparent combines the Latin prefix trans with the stem par, to appear, and adds -ent as an adjective ending.
intro.cn: transparent 把拉丁前缀 trans 与词干 par（显现）结合，并以 -ent 作形容词结尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin parere, to appear, also gives apparent and the verb appear, all built on the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 parere（显现）还生出 apparent 与动词 appear，都建在同一词干上。

items.example: It tells us the light passes through.
items.exampleCN: 它告诉我们光穿了过去。

items.example: The stem gives the idea of showing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干给出显现的意思。

items.example: It makes the stem an adjective.
It forms transparency, the state of being clear.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 transparency，透明的状态。

items.example: It forms transparently, in a clear way.
The same stem appears here without trans.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干在这里出现，只是没有 trans。

items.example: The verb keeps the plain sense of showing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词保留了显现的朴素含义。
它构成 semi-transparent，部分透明的。

definition_zh: 辛辣的；加香料的；刺激劲爆的
definition_en: having a strong hot flavour from spices, or exciting in content
core_image: 红辣椒在热锅里爆出呛人的香气
scene: 这道汤对孩子们来说太辣了。 The soup is too spicy for the children.
sceneCN: 这里 spicy 是「辛辣的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这道汤对孩子们来说太辣了。

senses.title: Hot to the tongue
senses.definition: having a hot, strong taste from spices
senses.definitionCN: 因香料而有强烈辣味的
senses.example: The curry is too spicy for me.
senses.exampleCN: 这份咖喱对我来说太辣了。
senses.why: The core sense is physical heat on the tongue.
senses.whyCN: 最核心的用法，指食物入口发辣。

senses.title: Full of spice aroma
senses.definition: flavoured or scented with spice
senses.definitionCN: 用香料调味或加香的
senses.example: The kitchen smelled spicy and warm.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房里弥漫着温暖而辛香的气味。
senses.why: This sense stresses scent rather than heat.
senses.whyCN: 强调香料带来的香气，而不只是辣。

senses.title: Slightly shocking
senses.definition: exciting and slightly shocking in content
senses.definitionCN: 内容刺激而略带劲爆的
senses.example: The paper printed a spicy story about the actor.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸刊登了一则关于那位演员的劲爆故事。
senses.why: The taste of heat is borrowed for exciting content.
senses.whyCN: 由味觉的刺激引申到内容令人兴奋。

intro.en: Spicy is spice plus the adjective suffix -y.
intro.cn: spicy 由 spice 加形容词后缀 -y 构成。

items.en: Species meant appearance and later a kind of goods.
items.cn: species 意为外观，后指某一类货物。

items.en: Espice named an aromatic plant product.
items.cn: espice 指芳香的植物制品。

items.en: Spice entered English as a word for such goods.
items.cn: spice 进入英语，指这类货物。

items.en: Spicy first described food full of spice.
items.cn: spicy 最初形容香料充足的食物。

items.en: It later extended to exciting stories and gossip.
items.cn: 后来扩展到劲爆的故事与八卦。

note.en: Spicy is compared with look-alike words and words for hot flavours.
note.cn: 把 spicy 与形近词以及表示辛辣味道的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Spicy is what spice does to your tongue.
normalIntro.cn: spicy 就是香料在舌头上做的事。

normal.en: I love spicy noodles.
normal.cn: 我喜欢辣面。

normal.en: The sauce is too spicy.
normal.cn: 这酱太辣了。

normal.en: Spicy food makes me sweat.
normal.cn: 辣的食物让我出汗。

normal.en: The kitchen smelled spicy.
normal.cn: 厨房里满是香料味。

normal.en: The magazine loves spicy stories.
normal.cn: 这本杂志喜欢劲爆的故事。

abstract.en: Spicy is heat you can taste.
abstract.cn: 辣，是尝得到的温度。

abstract.en: A little spice wakes a dull dish.
abstract.cn: 一点香料，能叫醒一道寡淡的菜。

abstract.en: The hottest dishes are remembered longest.
abstract.cn: 最辣的菜，记得最久。

examples.en: The curry is too spicy for me.
examples.cn: 这份咖喱对我来说太辣了。

examples.en: The kitchen smelled spicy and warm.
examples.cn: 厨房里弥漫着温暖而辛香的气味。

examples.en: The paper printed a spicy story about the actor.
examples.cn: 报纸刊登了一则关于那位演员的劲爆故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: spicy 由 spice（香料）加 -y 构成；比较级 spicier、最高级 spiciest；spicy food 是「辛辣食物」，spicy story 是「劲爆故事」；注意与 specify 区分。

root: 来自拉丁语 species（外观、种类），经古法语 espice 指香料，加后缀 -y 构成形容词，核心义由「多香料的」扩展到「刺激的」。

sensesIntro.en: Spicy means hot with spice, full of spice aroma, or exciting in content.
sensesIntro.cn: spicy 指食物辛辣、香气浓郁，或内容刺激劲爆。

core.en: Heat borrowed from plants.
core.cn: 向植物借来的热。

branches.en: A red pepper is cut into a hot pan.
branches.cn: 红辣椒被切进热锅。

branches.en: Steam carries the scent through the kitchen.
branches.cn: 蒸汽把香气带满厨房。

branches.en: A reader turns a page with wide eyes.
branches.cn: 读者睁大眼睛翻过一页。

branches.en: Heat and scent rise from the same seed.
branches.cn: 辣与香，来自同一粒种子。

branches.en: What teases the nose can also tease the mind.
branches.cn: 撩动鼻子的，也能撩动心思。

intro.en: Spicy builds comparison forms and related nouns.
intro.cn: spicy 构成比较级和相关名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is species, appearance or kind.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 species，意为外观或种类。

items.example: It is the spiciest dish here.
Add a little spice to the soup.

items.exampleCN: 他们端上了加香料的茶。

definition_en: a long thin animal with no legs, to move in curves, or a person who cannot be trusted
core_image: 一条长蛇在草丛里蜿蜒滑行
scene: 一条蛇滑过草丛。 A snake slid through the grass.
sceneCN: 这里 snake 是「蛇」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一条蛇滑过草丛。

senses.title: Long legless animal
senses.definition: a long thin animal with no legs that moves by sliding
senses.definitionCN: 一种细长无腿、靠滑行移动的动物
senses.example: A snake slid through the grass.
senses.exampleCN: 一条蛇滑过草丛。
senses.why: This is the animal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是动物义项。

senses.title: Move in curves
senses.definition: to move in long curves like a snake
senses.definitionCN: 像蛇一样沿长长的曲线移动
senses.example: The road snakes along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路沿着海岸蜿蜒。
senses.why: The animal's movement became a verb.
senses.whyCN: 这种动物的移动方式变成了动词。

senses.title: Untrustworthy person
senses.definition: a person who is dangerous and cannot be trusted
senses.definitionCN: 危险且不可信任的人
senses.example: He turned out to be a snake.
senses.exampleCN: 结果他是个阴险的人。
senses.why: The animal's image carries a warning.
senses.whyCN: 这种动物的形象带有警示意味。

intro.en: Snake comes from an Old English word for the animal.
intro.cn: snake 来自古英语中表示这种动物的词。

items.en: Snaca meant snake.
items.cn: snaca 意为蛇。

items.en: The word became snake.
items.cn: 词形演变为 snake。

items.en: It named the animal.
items.cn: 它指这种动物。

items.en: The verb meant to move in curves.
items.cn: 动词义为弯曲前进。

items.en: The word could describe a false person.
items.cn: 这个词也能形容虚伪的人。

note.en: Snake is compared with look-alike words and other reptiles.
note.cn: 把 snake 与形近词以及其他爬行动物作比较。

normalIntro.en: A snake is a long curve that can warn or threaten.
normalIntro.cn: snake 是既可能警示也可能威胁的长曲线。

normal.en: A snake slid through the grass.
normal.cn: 一条蛇滑过草丛。

normal.en: The road snakes along the coast.
normal.cn: 这条路沿着海岸蜿蜒。

normal.en: He turned out to be a snake.
normal.cn: 结果他是个阴险的人。

normal.en: The snake charmer played a pipe.
normal.cn: 耍蛇人吹起了笛子。

normal.en: A grass snake is harmless to people.
normal.cn: 草蛇对人无害。

abstract.en: A snake has no legs but never loses its way.
abstract.cn: 蛇没有腿，却从不迷路。

abstract.en: Some dangers arrive in a beautiful curve.
abstract.cn: 有些危险以美丽的曲线到来。

abstract.en: The word snake teaches that shape can carry judgment.
abstract.cn: snake 这个词说明形状也能承载评判。

examples.en: A snake slid through the grass.
examples.cn: 一条蛇滑过草丛。

examples.en: The road snakes along the coast.
examples.cn: 这条路沿着海岸蜿蜒。

examples.en: He turned out to be a snake.
examples.cn: 结果他是个阴险的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: snake 与 snack、stake 形近；snake in the grass 是「潜伏的敌人」，snake its way 是「蜿蜒而行」。

root: 由古英语 snaca（蛇）演变而来，核心义「细长蜿蜒之物」。

sensesIntro.en: Snake is the animal, a curving movement, or an untrustworthy person.
sensesIntro.cn: snake 指蛇、蜿蜒的动作，或不可信任的人。

core.en: A long thin curve that slides.
core.cn: 滑行的细长曲线。

branches.en: The animal moves without legs.
branches.cn: 这种动物无腿而行。

branches.en: A road copies the animal's curve.
branches.cn: 道路模仿这种动物的曲线。

branches.en: A false friend borrows the image.
branches.cn: 虚伪的朋友借用了这个形象。

branches.en: Animal and road share one shape.
branches.cn: 动物与道路共享同一形状。

branches.en: The curve can charm or deceive.
branches.cn: 曲线能迷人也能欺骗。

intro.en: Snake builds words for the animal and snake-like things.
intro.cn: snake 构成表示这种动物及蛇状物的词。

latinIntro.en: Snake is a native English word, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: snake 是英语本族词，不是拉丁语。

items.example: The snake disappeared into the leaves.
The line snaked around the block.

items.exampleCN: 一条蜿蜒的小路通向山上。

items.example: The river has a snaky bend.
items.exampleCN: 这条河有一处蛇形弯道。

items.example: A snake-like creature moved in the water.
items.exampleCN: 一个蛇形的生物在水中移动。

items.example: He was treated for a snakebite.
The boots were made of snakeskin.

definition_zh: 拱；拱门；足弓；拱起；首要的（构词前缀义）
definition_en: a curved structure that spans an opening and supports weight above it, or a curved shape resembling this
core_image: 一块块楔形石互相挤压，把上方的重量沿曲线传到两侧墙脚
scene: 石桥下的圆弧把整条桥面托住，石缝里长着细草。 The stone arch carries the weight of the wall above it without any wooden beam.
sceneCN: 这里 arch 指「跨越开口并把上方重量分散到两侧的拱形结构」（第 1 个义项：拱）；句意为这道石拱不用木梁就承住了上方的墙。图中可辨识物件：石桥、圆弧、楔形石、墙脚。

pos.zh: 首要的；为首的（多作构词成分）

senses.title: A curved spanning structure
senses.definition: a curved structure that spans an opening and carries weight by compression
senses.definitionCN: 跨越开口、靠受压传递重量的曲线结构
senses.example: The arch turns the downward load into a sideways thrust.
senses.exampleCN: 拱把向下的荷载转为向两侧的推力。
senses.why: the word first named a bow, and a bent bow is exactly the shape that carries weight by compression.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指弓，而弯弓正是靠受压承重的形状。

senses.title: A gateway with a curved top
senses.definition: an opening in a wall topped by a curve, often built as a monument
senses.definitionCN: 墙上的曲线顶开口，常作为纪念性建筑
senses.example: The triumphal arch marks the old entrance to the city.
senses.exampleCN: 那座凯旋门标记着城市的旧入口。
senses.why: when the structure is mostly an opening, the word names the gateway rather than the engineering.
senses.whyCN: 当结构主要是一个开口时，这个词指门本身，而非工程原理。

senses.title: The arch of the foot
senses.definition: the curved instep of the human foot, formed by bones and ligaments
senses.definitionCN: 由骨骼与韧带形成的人脚背曲线
senses.example: The arch of the foot acts as a spring with every step.
senses.exampleCN: 每走一步，足弓都像弹簧一样工作。
senses.why: the body has its own spanning curves, so the architectural word was applied to anatomy.
senses.whyCN: 身体自身就有跨度的曲线，因此建筑词被用到解剖上。

senses.title: The brow's curve
senses.definition: the bony ridge above the eye
senses.definitionCN: 眼睛上方的骨质隆起
senses.example: A heavy arch above the eyes gives the skull a stern look.
senses.exampleCN: 眼睛上方厚重的眉弓让头骨显得严厉。
senses.why: any bony curve can be called an arch, and the brow is the most visible one.
senses.whyCN: 任何骨质曲线都可叫 arch，而眉弓是最显眼的一处。

senses.title: Anything shaped like a bow
senses.definition: a curved object or line, such as a rainbow or a row of trees
senses.definitionCN: 弯曲的物体或线条，如彩虹或一排行道树
senses.example: A pale arch of light stood over the valley after the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后，一道浅色光弧立在山谷上方。
senses.why: the shape sense is older than the building sense and survives in descriptions of nature.
senses.whyCN: 形状义比建筑义更古老，并在自然描写中留存。

senses.title: To curve upward or over
senses.definition: to bend into a curve, or to span something in a curve
senses.definitionCN: 弯成曲线，或以曲线跨越某物
senses.example: The cat arched its back at the sound of the door.
senses.exampleCN: 听到门响，猫弓起了背。
senses.why: the verb is simply the shape turned into motion, and it applies to bodies, branches and eyebrows.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把形状变成动作，适用于身体、枝条与眉毛。

senses.title: Chief or principal
senses.definition: in compounds, first or foremost, as in arch-enemy or arch-criminal
senses.definitionCN: 在复合词中表示第一位的、为首的，如头号敌人或首恶
senses.example: He became the arch-rival of the reigning champion.
senses.exampleCN: 他成了在位冠军的头号对手。
senses.why: this sense has a different source: a Greek word for leader, not the Latin word for bow.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来源不同：它来自希腊语「首领」，而非拉丁语「弓」。

senses.title: A shoe's arch support
senses.definition: the raised part inside a shoe that supports the instep
senses.definitionCN: 鞋内托住脚背的隆起部分
senses.example: The insole's arch takes the pressure off the heel.
senses.exampleCN: 鞋垫的足弓部分减轻了脚跟压力。
senses.why: shoemaking borrowed the anatomical word for the part of the foot it must hold.
senses.whyCN: 制鞋业借用了这个解剖词，指它必须托住的那部分脚。

intro.en: English arch is two words that look alike: a Latin bow and a Greek leader. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 英语 arch 是两个形似的词：一个来自拉丁语「弓」，一个来自希腊语「首领」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Arcus meant a bow or a curved arc, and it named both the weapon and the shape.
items.cn: arcus 指弓或弧线，既命名武器也命名形状。

items.en: Old French arche carried the architectural sense into English, where it named a curved span.
items.cn: 古法语 arche 把建筑义带入英语，指曲线跨度。

items.en: Separately, Greek arkhos meant leader or chief, and its combining form entered English as a prefix.
items.cn: 另一方面，希腊语 arkhos 意为首领，其组合形式作为前缀进入英语。

items.en: From the twelfth century the pointed and round arch drove Gothic and Romanesque building.
items.cn: 从十二世纪起，尖拱与圆拱推动了哥特式与罗曼式建筑。

items.en: The same shape word was applied to the instep and the brow because both are curved supports.
items.cn: 同一个形状词被用于脚背与眉部，因为两者都是曲线支撑。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin ancestry of arcus is not established, and the Greek leader word has a separate disputed origin, so the two are not related despite identical spelling.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：arcus 在拉丁语之前的谱系未得到证明，希腊语「首领」词另有争议来源；两者拼写相同但并无亲缘关系。

note.en: Group one holds words from the Latin bow family or easily mistaken for them; group two holds curved structures and shapes.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「弓」一族或容易误认的词；第二组是曲线结构与形状。

entries.definition: A part of a circle, or an electric discharge across a gap; both come from the same Latin bow word.
entries.definitionCN: 圆周的一段，或跨越间隙的放电；两义都来自同一个拉丁「弓」词。

entries.definition: A person who shoots with a bow; it comes from the same Latin source but names a person.
entries.definitionCN: 用弓射箭的人；同出拉丁来源，但指人。

entries.definition: A prefix meaning chief, from Greek; it is unrelated to the Latin bow and must be read separately.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「首领」的前缀，来自希腊语；与拉丁「弓」无关，须分开理解。

entries.definition: A passage under an arch; it is arch plus way, a covered route rather than the structure alone.
entries.definitionCN: 拱下的通道；由 arch 加 way 构成，指有顶路线而非单独结构。

entries.definition: An arched ceiling over a space; an arch spans an opening in a wall, while a vault covers a room.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖空间的拱形顶棚；arch 跨越墙上的开口，vault 覆盖房间。

entries.definition: A curved roof over a round space; it is an arch rotated around a centre.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖圆形空间的曲面屋顶；是绕中心旋转的拱。

entries.definition: A straight structural member carrying load; it works by bending, while an arch works by compression.
entries.definitionCN: 承受荷载的直构件，靠弯曲工作；而拱靠受压工作。

entries.definition: Any line that bends; an arch is one kind of curve with a structural job.
entries.definitionCN: 任何弯曲的线；arch 是带有结构任务的一种曲线。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real bow root, the real anatomy words and the separate Greek prefix.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「弓」词根、真实的解剖词与另一个希腊语前缀。

normal.en: The Latin root means bow, so the structure and the weapon share one curved shape.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根意为弓，因此结构与武器共有一个弯曲的形状。

normal.en: The family runs arch, arched, archer, archery, archway, archwise.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 arch、arched、archer、archery、archway、archwise。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: stone arch, arch bridge, arch of the foot, arch enemy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各分支：石拱、拱桥、足弓、头号敌人。

normal.en: The curve works by squeezing: each stone pushes its neighbour and the load slides down the legs.
normal.cn: 这条曲线靠挤压工作：每块石头推着邻石，荷载沿两侧墙脚滑下。

normal.en: The chief sense is a different word: Greek leader, not Latin bow.
normal.cn: 「首要」义是另一个词：希腊语首领，而非拉丁语弓。

abstract.en: Picture a row of stones learning to lean on each other so none falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一排石头学会彼此倚靠，于是一块也不落。

abstract.en: Picture a rainbow that has been asked to hold up a bridge.
abstract.cn: 想象一道彩虹被请求去托住一座桥。

abstract.en: Picture an eyebrow as a small bridge over an eye.
abstract.cn: 想象眉毛是一只眼睛上方的小桥。

examples.en: The bridge's arch has stood for six hundred years.
examples.cn: 这座桥的拱已立了六百年。

examples.en: High arches support the soles of runners.
examples.cn: 高足弓支撑着跑者的脚底。

examples.en: The two companies are arch rivals in the same market.
examples.cn: 这两家公司在同一市场是头号对手。

dict_mnemonic.text: arcus（弓）→ 弯成弓形的承重结构 → 拱；同形前缀又表示「首领」

root: 名词 arch 来自拉丁 arcus「弓、弧」，经古法语 arche 入英语；表示「首领」的 arch- 另有希腊语 arkhos 来源，二者拼写相同但无亲缘。英语 arch。arcus 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one curve: a bow becomes a span, then a gateway, then the body's own arches, then any curved shape, a verb, a separate 'chief' prefix and finally a shoe part.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条曲线展开：弓成为跨度，再成为门、身体自身的弓、任何弯曲形状、动词，另有一条「首领」前缀义，最后落到鞋内支撑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wedge-shaped stones leaning on one another so the load travels down both legs.
core.cn: 核心意象：楔形石块彼此倚靠，使荷载沿两侧墙脚传下。

branches.en: THE CURVE: a structural span and a rainbow are the same bowed line with and without a job.
branches.cn: 曲线：承重跨度与彩虹，是同一条弓形线，一条有任务，一条没有。

branches.en: THE GATEWAY: when the opening matters more than the engineering, the arch becomes a door.
branches.cn: 门：当开口比工程更重要时，拱就成了门。

branches.en: THE BODY: the foot, the brow and the shoe all repeat the same small bridge.
branches.cn: 身体：脚、眉与鞋都重复着同一座小桥。

branches.en: THE ACTION: the shape becomes a verb when a back or a branch bends.
branches.cn: 动作：当背或枝条弯曲时，形状变成动词。

branches.en: THE OTHER WORD: the 'chief' sense is a Greek leader, not a Latin bow.
branches.cn: 另一个词：「首要」义是希腊语首领，而非拉丁语弓。

intro.en: Arch is a Latin bow noun plus a separate Greek leader prefix, so the affix list must keep the two lines apart.
intro.cn: arch 是一个拉丁语「弓」名词加上一个独立的希腊语「首领」前缀，因此词缀清单必须把两条线分开。

latinIntro.en: Latin arcus gives arc, arch, archer and archery; the prefix arch- comes from Greek arkhos and is not a relative.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 arcus 给出 arc、arch、archer 与 archery；表示「首领」的前缀来自希腊语 arkhos，并非同族。

items.example: Arcus named the weapon and the curve.
items.exampleCN: 这个词既指武器也指曲线。

items.example: The arc of the bridge is shallow.
An arched window lights the stair.

items.meaning: the sport of shooting with a bow

items.example: The archway leads to the courtyard.
An arch-rival is the chief rival.
items.exampleCN: 头号对手就是最主要的对手。

definition_en: to break in on someone who is speaking or doing something, or to stop something from continuing
core_image: 一条拉直的线被剪刀从中间剪断，两头各自翘起
scene: 会议进行到一半，门被推开，有人急着插话报告消息。 Sorry to interrupt, but the train has been cancelled.
sceneCN: 这里 interrupt 是「打断」（第 1 个义项：插进别人正在说的话里），句意为抱歉打扰，但那班火车已取消。画面里的物件：半开的门、会议桌、手机。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「中断；打扰」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「被打断的」
加前缀 un- 构成，义为「不间断的」
同一词根 rumpere 构成，义为「突然的」

senses.title: Break into speech
senses.definition: to start speaking while someone else is still talking
senses.definitionCN: 在别人还在说话时开口插话
senses.example: Please do not interrupt while the witness is answering.
senses.exampleCN: 证人回答时请不要打断。
senses.why: Latin rumpere means to break; inter- means between, so the word breaks in between.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rumpere 意为「折断」，inter- 意为「之间」，合起来就是「从中间插进去」。

senses.title: Stop a process
senses.definition: to cause an activity or process to stop before it is finished
senses.definitionCN: 使某项活动或过程在完成前停止
senses.example: Heavy snow interrupted the power supply for two days.
senses.exampleCN: 大雪使供电中断了两天。
senses.why: The break image moves from conversation to machinery and weather.
senses.whyCN: 「折断」的图像从对话转到机器与天气上。

senses.title: Block a view or line
senses.definition: to block something that would otherwise be continuous, such as a view or a path
senses.definitionCN: 遮断本来是连续的东西，如视线或通路
senses.example: A new tower interrupts the view from the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 一座新楼挡住了从桥上望出去的景色。
senses.why: Anything that cuts a line counts as an interruption, even in space.
senses.whyCN: 凡是把一条线切断的事都算打断，即使发生在空间里。

intro.en: Interrupt is built from Latin inter- "between" and rumpere "to break".
intro.cn: interrupt 由拉丁语 inter-「之间」与 rumpere「折断」构成。

items.en: Rumpere meant to break or burst a solid thing.
items.cn: rumpere 意为折断或使坚硬之物破裂。

items.en: Interrumpere meant to break something in the middle.
items.cn: interrumpere 意为从中间把某物折断。

items.en: The participle interruptus described a broken-off state.
items.cn: 分词 interruptus 描述被切断的状态。

items.en: English borrowed interrupt in the fifteenth century for broken speech.
items.cn: 英语十五世纪借入 interrupt，指被打断的话语。

items.en: The word spread to power, travel, and any halted process.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到供电、交通以及一切被停下的过程。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -rupt root; the near-meaning group holds other ways of cutting in.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -rupt 词根；近义组收其他「插进来」的说法。

entries.definition: The act or an instance of breaking in.
To burst out, as a volcano does.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「爆发」，同出 rumpere。

entries.definition: Rotten or dishonest, literally broken through.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「腐败的」，字面是「被彻底破坏」。

entries.definition: To trouble someone's quiet or work.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「打扰」，强调扰乱安宁。

entries.definition: To join a conversation without being asked.
To stop suddenly in the middle.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语义为「突然中断」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of a line snapped in two.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子守着「一条线被剪成两截」的画面。

normal.en: inter- between plus rupt break equals breaking in between.
normal.cn: inter-「之间」加 rupt「折断」等于从中间插断。

normal.en: A rupt root shows up in erupt and corrupt too.
normal.cn: rupt 词根也出现在 erupt 与 corrupt 里。

normal.en: Sorry to interrupt is the polite door knock of speech.
normal.cn: sorry to interrupt 是话语世界里礼貌的敲门声。

normal.en: An uninterrupted film runs from start to end.
normal.cn: uninterrupted 的影片从头放到尾。

normal.en: Snow can interrupt a journey far more rudely than a person.
normal.cn: 雪比人更不讲礼地打断一段行程。

abstract.en: An interruption is a line that refuses to stay straight.
abstract.cn: 打断就是一条不肯保持笔直的线。

abstract.en: Every conversation is two people taking turns not to snap.
abstract.cn: 每场对话都是两个人轮流克制着不去剪断。

abstract.en: To interrupt is to borrow time you have not been given.
abstract.cn: 打断是借用一段没人给你的时间。

examples.en: She interrupted his story to ask a question.
examples.cn: 她打断他的讲述，问了一个问题。

examples.en: The strike interrupted production for three weeks.
examples.cn: 罢工使生产中断了三周。

examples.en: Do not interrupt the machine while it is updating.
examples.cn: 机器更新时不要中断它。

dict_mnemonic.text: inter（之间）+ rupt（断）——从中间把它断开

root: 拉丁语 inter「之间」+ rumpere「折断」→ interrumpere「从中间打断」→ 英语 interrupt。同族有 interruption、erupt、corrupt。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: break into speech, stop a process, and cut across a view or path.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：插话、中断过程、遮断视线或通路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight line cut in the middle by a scissor.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条直线被剪刀从中间剪开。

branches.en: THE VOICE: one speaker cutting into another.
branches.cn: 嗓音这条线：一个人插进另一个人的话。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: a process stopped before its end.
branches.cn: 机器这条线：过程在结束前被停住。

branches.en: THE VIEW: something placed across a line of sight.
branches.cn: 视线这条线：有东西横在目光前面。

branches.en: THE LINK: both senses break a flow that was running.
branches.cn: 连接线：两个义项都截断了一股正在流动的东西。

branches.en: THE BARRIER: stopping and blocking share the same snap.
branches.cn: 屏障线：停止与遮挡共用同一次折断。

intro.en: Interrupt is inter- "between" plus the Latin root rupt- "break".
intro.cn: interrupt 是 inter-「之间」加拉丁词根 rupt-「折断」。

latinIntro.en: Latin rumpere, interrumpere and the participle interruptus are all recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rumpere、interrumpere 与分词 interruptus 均有记载。

items.example: It puts the break in the middle.
The root also lives in rupture.
The verb is the base of the root.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词根的基础。

items.example: The participle gave the English verb its shape.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词给了英语动词形式。
它构成 erupt，意为向外爆出。
它构成 corrupt，意为被彻底毁坏。

definition_en: very brave, like a hero, or grand in scale
core_image: 比常人高出半头、迎着危险站定的身影
scene: 她冲进着火的房子救孩子，十分英勇。 Her rush into the burning house to save the child was heroic.
sceneCN: 这里 heroic 是「英勇的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她冲进着火的房子救孩子，十分英勇。

senses.title: Very brave
senses.definition: showing great courage
senses.definitionCN: 表现出巨大勇气的
senses.example: Her rush into the burning house was heroic.
senses.exampleCN: 她冲进着火的房子，十分英勇。
senses.why: This is the main sense of courage.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示勇气的主要义项。

senses.title: Grand in scale
senses.definition: large and grand, like the deeds in old epics
senses.definitionCN: 宏大壮丽，像古代史诗中的事迹
senses.example: The novel tells a heroic story of the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说讲述了一个史诗般的海洋故事。
senses.why: Epic stories gave the word its grand sense.
senses.whyCN: 史诗故事赋予这个词宏大的含义。

senses.title: Huge effort
senses.definition: needing great effort to succeed
senses.definitionCN: 需要付出巨大努力才能成功的
senses.example: They made a heroic effort to finish on time.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为按时完成付出了艰苦卓绝的努力。
senses.why: Great effort looks like a hero's labour.
senses.whyCN: 巨大的努力看起来像英雄的劳作。

intro.en: Heroic comes from the Greek word for a hero.
intro.cn: heroic 来自希腊语中表示英雄的词。

items.en: Heros meant a demigod or warrior.
items.cn: heros 意为半神或战士。

items.en: Heroicus meant belonging to a hero.
items.cn: heroicus 意为属于英雄的。

items.en: Heroique described brave deeds.
items.cn: heroique 形容英勇的事迹。

items.en: Heroic described brave people and acts.
items.cn: heroic 形容勇敢的人和行为。

items.en: Heroic also described grand epic style.
items.cn: heroic 也形容宏大的史诗风格。

note.en: Heroic is compared with look-alike words and with words for courage.
note.cn: 把 heroic 与形近词以及表示勇敢的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Heroic is what a hero does, and what an epic story feels like.
normalIntro.cn: heroic 既是英雄所做的，也是史诗故事给人的感觉。

normal.en: Her rush into the burning house was heroic.
normal.cn: 她冲进着火的房子，十分英勇。

normal.en: The novel tells a heroic story of the sea.
normal.cn: 这部小说讲述了一个史诗般的海洋故事。

normal.en: They made a heroic effort to finish on time.
normal.cn: 他们为按时完成付出了艰苦卓绝的努力。

normal.en: The statue shows a heroic figure on horseback.
normal.cn: 雕像展现了一位骑马的英雄人物。

normal.en: It was a heroic struggle against the flood.
normal.cn: 那是与洪水的一场英勇斗争。

abstract.en: Heroic deeds are often quiet until someone tells them.
abstract.cn: 英雄事迹在被讲述之前，往往是安静的。

abstract.en: To be heroic is to pay a price others avoid.
abstract.cn: 英勇，就是付出别人回避的代价。

abstract.en: The heroic age ends when people stop looking up.
abstract.cn: 当人们不再仰望，英雄时代就结束了。

examples.en: Her rush into the burning house to save the child was heroic.
examples.cn: 她冲进着火的房子救孩子，十分英勇。

examples.en: They made a heroic effort to finish on time.
examples.cn: 他们为按时完成付出了艰苦卓绝的努力。

examples.en: The novel tells a heroic story of the sea.
examples.cn: 这部小说讲述了一个史诗般的海洋故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: heroic 是「英勇的」，也可形容规模宏大或努力艰苦；heroic effort 是英勇的努力，heroic struggle 是英勇斗争，heroic figure 是英雄人物。

root: 来自希腊语 heros（英雄），经拉丁语 heroicus 与法语 heroique 进入英语；由英雄具备的勇气，引申为英勇的，再形容史诗般的宏大和需要巨大努力的事。

sensesIntro.en: Heroic means very brave, grand like an epic, or requiring huge effort.
sensesIntro.cn: heroic 表示非常勇敢、像史诗般宏大，或需要巨大努力。

core.en: The height of courage, seen from below.
core.cn: 从下方仰望的勇气高度。

branches.en: Her rush into the burning house was heroic.
branches.cn: 她冲进着火的房子，十分英勇。

branches.en: The novel tells a heroic story of the sea.
branches.cn: 这部小说讲述了一个史诗般的海洋故事。

branches.en: They made a heroic effort to finish on time.
branches.cn: 他们为按时完成付出了艰苦卓绝的努力。

branches.en: Real courage and epic stories share the same word.
branches.cn: 真实的勇气和史诗故事共用一个词。

branches.en: A heroic act is usually a huge effort first.
branches.cn: 英勇之举，往往先是一份巨大的努力。

intro.en: Heroic takes -ally, and shares its base with hero and heroine.
intro.cn: heroic 可加 -ally，并与 hero、heroine 同根。

latinIntro.en: The base comes from Greek through Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的基形来自希腊语，经拉丁语传入。

items.exampleCN: 他们赞扬他的英雄气概。

items.example: She is the heroine of the film.
items.exampleCN: 她是这部电影的女主角。

items.example: Enough heroics, we need a plan.
items.exampleCN: 别逞英雄了，我们需要计划。
他们付出了英勇的努力。

items.example: The poem uses the heroic couplet.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗采用英雄双韵体。

latinEntries.example: Heroicus gave English the word heroic.
latinEntries.exampleCN: heroicus 演变为英语的 heroic。

definition_en: an amount left over after what is needed has been used
core_image: 仓库里堆着多出来的粮食袋，标签写着剩余
scene: 今年的收成有剩余，可以卖给邻村。 This year's harvest left a surplus that could be sold to the next village.
sceneCN: 这里 surplus 是「剩余」（第 1 个义项）；句意：今年的收成有剩余，可以卖给邻村。

senses.title: An amount left over
senses.definition: an amount that remains after needs are met
senses.definitionCN: 满足需求后剩下的数量
senses.example: This year's harvest left a surplus that could be sold to the next village.
senses.exampleCN: 今年的收成有剩余，可以卖给邻村。
senses.why: This is the basic sense of something left over.
senses.whyCN: 这是「剩下之物」的基本义项。

senses.title: A financial gain
senses.definition: the amount by which income is greater than spending
senses.definitionCN: 收入大于支出的部分
senses.example: The government reported a budget surplus.
senses.exampleCN: 政府报告了预算盈余。
senses.why: In finance the leftover becomes a positive balance.
senses.whyCN: 在财政中，剩余变成正结余。

intro.en: Surplus joins the Latin words for above and more.
intro.cn: surplus 把拉丁语中表示「在上」和「更多」的词结合起来。

items.en: Super meant above.
items.cn: super 意为在上。

items.en: Plus meant more.
items.cn: plus 意为更多。

items.en: Surplus meant something extra.
items.cn: surplus 意为多余之物。

items.en: Surplus named an amount left over.
items.cn: surplus 指剩余的数量。

items.en: Surplus extended to budget and trade balances.
items.cn: surplus 扩展到预算与贸易结余。

note.en: Surplus is compared with look-alike words and with words for extra amounts.
note.cn: 把 surplus 与形近词以及表示多余数量的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Surplus is what remains above what was needed.
normalIntro.cn: surplus 是超出所需而剩下的部分。

normal.en: This year's harvest left a surplus that could be sold to the next village.
normal.cn: 今年的收成有剩余，可以卖给邻村。

normal.en: The government reported a budget surplus.
normal.cn: 政府报告了预算盈余。

normal.en: The country runs a trade surplus with its neighbours.
normal.cn: 该国与邻国保持贸易顺差。

normal.en: Surplus goods were stored in the old barn.
normal.cn: 剩余物资存放在旧谷仓里。

normal.en: A surplus of teachers filled the hall.
normal.cn: 多余的教师挤满了大厅。

abstract.en: Surplus is the quiet proof that a system produced more than it needed.
abstract.cn: 剩余是一个体系产出多于所需的无声证明。

abstract.en: What is extra for one place may be missing in another.
abstract.cn: 对一地多余的东西，在另一地可能正缺。

abstract.en: The word adds plus to super and turns abundance into a quantity.
abstract.cn: 这个词把 plus 加到 super 上，把丰足变成一个数量。

examples.en: This year's harvest left a surplus that could be sold to the next village.
examples.cn: 今年的收成有剩余，可以卖给邻村。

examples.en: The government reported a budget surplus.
examples.cn: 政府报告了预算盈余。

examples.en: Surplus goods were stored in the old barn.
examples.cn: 剩余物资存放在旧谷仓里。

dict_mnemonic.text: super 表示「超过」，plus 表示「更多」，surplus 就是多出来的部分，即剩余、盈余。

root: 源自拉丁语 super（在上）与 plus（更多），经古法语 surplus 进入英语，指超出所需的部分。

sensesIntro.en: Surplus means an amount left over, or a positive balance of income over spending.
sensesIntro.cn: surplus 指剩余数量，也指收入大于支出的盈余。

core.en: More than the need, left in hand.
core.cn: 多于所需而留在手里的部分。

branches.en: This year's harvest left a surplus that could be sold to the next village.
branches.cn: 今年的收成有剩余，可以卖给邻村。

branches.en: Surplus goods were stored in the old barn.
branches.cn: 剩余物资存放在旧谷仓里。

branches.en: The government reported a budget surplus.
branches.cn: 政府报告了预算盈余。

branches.en: Corn left over and money left over share one word.
branches.cn: 剩下的粮食与剩下的钱共用一个词。

branches.en: The country runs a trade surplus with its neighbours.
branches.cn: 该国与邻国保持贸易顺差。

intro.en: Surplus forms surpluses and relates to plus and super.
intro.cn: surplus 可构成复数 surpluses，并与 plus、super 相关。

latinIntro.en: Latin super and plus both survive in English as separate words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 super 与 plus 都作为独立词留在英语中。

items.example: The farm had surpluses for years.

items.exampleCN: super 在拉丁语中意为在上。

items.example: An excess of salt ruins soup.

definition_en: the act of saying words for someone to write down, or a test in which you write what is read
core_image: 教室里笔尖沙沙响，老师一句句慢慢念
scene: 教室里只听得见笔尖划纸的声音，老师念一句就停一下。 The class did a dictation of ten sentences.
sceneCN: 这里 dictation 指「听写」（第 2 个义项：把听到的话写下来的练习或测验）；句意是全班做了一次十句的听写。

senses.title: The act of speaking for a writer
senses.definition: the act of saying words aloud for someone else to write down
senses.definitionCN: 把话念出来让别人记录下来的行为
senses.example: She took dictation from the editor for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 她为编辑做了一小时口述记录。
senses.why: Two people share one text, one speaking and one writing.
senses.whyCN: 两个人共用一篇文字，一个说，一个写。

senses.title: A writing test from speech
senses.definition: a test in which learners write down words that are read aloud
senses.definitionCN: 学习者把念出来的词句写下来的一种测验
senses.example: The class did a dictation of ten sentences.
senses.exampleCN: 全班做了一次十句的听写。
senses.why: The ear is asked to prove that the hand can spell.
senses.whyCN: 耳朵被要求证明，那只手拼得对。

senses.title: The text read out
senses.definition: the words or passage that is read aloud to be written
senses.definitionCN: 被念出来供人记录的那段文字
senses.example: The teacher prepared a short dictation for Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 老师为周一准备了一段短听写材料。
senses.why: The passage is a script waiting for many hands to copy it.
senses.whyCN: 那段文字是一份等许多只手来抄的稿子。

intro.en: Dictation comes from Latin dictatio, from dictare, to say repeatedly, and English adopted it in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: dictation 来自拉丁语 dictatio，源自动词 dictare（反复说），十六世纪进入英语。

items.en: Dictare meant to say a thing over so that it could be written.
items.cn: dictare 指把一句话说上几遍，好让人写下来。

items.en: Dictatio named that act and the text produced by it.
items.cn: dictatio 指这个行为，也指由此产生的文字。

items.en: English dictation first described a clerk writing at another's voice.
items.cn: 英语 dictation 最初指职员听别人的声音记录。

items.en: Schools turned it into an exercise for teaching spelling.
items.cn: 学校把它变成教拼写的练习。

items.en: It now covers the act, the test and the passage read out.
items.cn: 如今它覆盖这个行为、测验以及念出来的那段文字。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dict stem, while the meaning group names ways of putting speech into writing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 dict 这个词干，近义组则指把话变成文字的各种方式。

entries.definition: to speak words for someone to write
a ruler who holds all power
entries.definitionCN: 掌握全部权力的统治者

entries.definition: a book of words and their meanings
a written copy of spoken words
the act of saying a text aloud
entries.definitionCN: 把一段文字念出来的行为

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with pens scratching in a quiet classroom and end with a sheet waiting for many hands.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从安静教室里沙沙的笔尖开始，落到一张等着许多手来抄的纸。

normal.en: Dictation is the noun of a voice handing words to a hand.
normal.cn: dictation 就是声音把词交给手的那个名词。

normal.en: In the classroom the ear must defend the spelling.
normal.cn: 在教室里，耳朵得为拼写作证。

normal.en: A clerk and a student do the same thing at different speeds.
normal.cn: 职员与学生做的是同一件事，只是速度不同。

normal.en: The text read out is a script before it is a test.
normal.cn: 念出来的文字，先是一份稿子，然后才是考题。

normal.en: One voice, many pens, one page.
normal.cn: 一把声音，许多支笔，一页纸。

abstract.en: Picture a row of desks all leaning over paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一排课桌，全都伏在纸上。

abstract.en: Picture a teacher pausing with one finger raised.
abstract.cn: 想象老师竖起一根手指停下。

abstract.en: Picture a mimeographed sheet passed down a row.
abstract.cn: 想象一张油印纸沿着一排传下去。

examples.en: She took dictation from the editor for an hour.
examples.cn: 她为编辑做了一小时口述记录。

examples.en: The class did a dictation of ten sentences.
examples.cn: 全班做了一次十句的听写。

examples.en: The teacher prepared a short dictation for Monday.
examples.cn: 老师为周一准备了一段短听写材料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dictation 记成「迪克推神」：dict 是说，-ation 是过程，把话一遍遍说出去让人记，就是口述与听写。

root: 来自拉丁语 dictatio，源自动词 dictare（反复说、规定），而 dictare 又来自 dicere（说）。十六世纪进入英语，最初指听人口述做记录，十九世纪被学校用作拼写练习，如今兼指口述行为、听写测验与听写材料。

sensesIntro.en: From a clerk writing at a voice, to a classroom test, to the passage that is read out.
sensesIntro.cn: 从职员听着声音记录，到课堂上的测验，再到被念出来的那段文字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one voice and many pens moving to the same beat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把声音与许多支笔，跟着同一个节拍走。

branches.en: The first sense is the working act of voice and hand.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是声音与手配合的工作过程。

branches.en: The second sense is that act turned into a test.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是这个过程变成了考试。

branches.en: The third sense is the text that was read out.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是被念出来的那段文字。

branches.en: Practice and examination use the same slow reading.
branches.cn: 练习与考试，用的是同一种慢速念读。

branches.en: The test and its material are two sides of one sheet.
branches.cn: 测验与它的材料，是一张纸的两面。

intro.en: Dictation belongs to a family about speaking, writing down and the authority of the spoken word.
intro.cn: dictation 属于一族词，关于说、记录以及口头话语的权威。

latinIntro.en: The base dicere means to say, and -ation turns the repeated saying into a process.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 dicere 意为说，后缀 -ation 把反复说变成一个过程。

items.meaning: the act or a written test
to speak words to be written
